title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre, 1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

Directed by Bonnie Duff

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: Intro to Survival Skills: Shelter, Fire and Knots
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/survival-skills/intro-survival-skills)**
**Spend a Saturday becoming someone who knows what to do.**
Join us for a hands-on beginner day in Copeland Forest with Kyle, a survival instructor with over a decade of experience. You'll pitch a shelter, light a fire without matches, carve with a knife and tie the knots that hold it all together.
This class is open to any adult, member or not. Come on your own or bring a friend. Most people at our classes arrive solo. Total beginners are welcome: Kyle starts from zero, and there's no hiking, just short walks into the trees to gather wood.
**Kit provided:** Tarps, saws, hatchets, loaner ferro rods and knives to borrow, plus your own tinder kit and a printed handout. Want your own ferro rod (+$10) or Mora knife (+$40) to keep? Add one when you book.
**Getting there:** Add the bus for $50 and we'll pick you up at Keele Station at 8am and drop you back around 6pm. Or drive yourself to the P1 parking lot in Copeland Forest, near Horseshoe Valley, about an hour and a half north of Toronto.
No membership needed. After you book, we'll email you the waiver to sign and your plan with directions, timings and a packing list.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Put a roof over your head:** Learn to pick a good spot and pitch a tarp two ways, the A-frame and the plow point, so you know how to stay dry when the weather turns.
**Light a fire without matches:** Catch a ferro rod spark on fluffed jute, build up through twigs to logs, split wood by batoning and carve feather sticks.
**Knots, knife work and a tripod grill:** Learn the taut-line hitch, slip knot and bowline, carve your own chopsticks, spoon or spatula, then lash a tripod and grill over the fire.
**Itinerary**
**08:00** \- Bus leaves Keele Station \(if you've added it\)
**10:00** \- Meet at location\, for a welcome\, safety talk and knife handling
**Late morning** \- Tarp shelters: the A\-frame and the plow point
**Lunch** \- Bring a packed lunch and eat around the fire
**Afternoon** \- Fire without matches: ferro rod\, jute\, batoning and feather sticks
**Late afternoon** \- Knots\, bush cutlery and a tripod grill
**16:00** \- Wrap up and head home
**18:00** \- Bus arrives back at Keele Station
**Event cost: $135+HST. $50 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/survival-skills/intro-survival-skills)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: 🍁🎄Fall Niagara Falls Hiking Day Trip — Trails, Dinner & Festival of Lights!!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
# 🍁🎄 Niagara Falls Fall Hiking Trip & Winter Festival of Lights! 🌈

🌦️ **RAIN OR SHINE!**

The adventure goes on, whether we're enjoying golden sunshine, crisp autumn air, or a little mist from the Falls. After a day of hiking, we'll finish with dinner and the spectacular Winter Festival of Lights! ✨

***

## 🥾 About the Trip

Let's escape the city for a full day of fresh air, friendship, and breathtaking scenery! We'll explore the natural side of Niagara Falls — less time in the tourist crowds, more trails, trees, and spectacular views.

We'll meet outside the **Fairmont Royal York on Front Street West**, travel together by GO Train to Niagara Falls, and make our way to **Niagara Glen Nature Reserve** for a hike among ancient boulders, winding forest paths, and the turquoise waters of the Niagara River.

The trail features stairs, uneven ground, elevation changes, and a climb back up out of the gorge. This is a proper hike, so please read the expectations below before signing up.

**A Special Guest Joining Us!**

We're excited to welcome Miles Howard, visiting us from Boston on November 14–15!

Miles is writing *HIKE EVERY CITY*, a book (coming in 2028) exploring urban hiking, community, and how exploring cities on foot brings people together. He also runs a similar urban hiking project in Boston called *Walking City Trails*.

He'll be joining us for both weekend outings, including Niagara Falls, to experience our group firsthand and meet our members.
Feel free to say hello, share your experiences, and chat with Miles if you'd like. No pressure, of course!

It's exciting to see our community getting noticed beyond Toronto. Let's give Miles a warm welcome!

***

## 🌲 The Trail Experience

Niagara Glen is a beautiful natural area carved into the Niagara Gorge over thousands of years. We'll follow forest trails, take photos, enjoy the fall colours, and experience a side of Niagara Falls that many visitors never see.

The planned hike is approximately **4 km**, although the terrain makes it more demanding than the distance might suggest. We'll have opportunities to pause and enjoy the scenery, but everyone needs to be prepared for the physical demands of the route.

### ⚠️🥾 IMPORTANT: HIKE EXPECTATIONS — PLEASE READ CAREFULLY 🥾⚠️

**This is a real hiking trail, not a casual walk.**
Before signing up, please be confident that you can:

* ✔️ Walk for an extended period of time.
* ✔️ Handle uneven terrain, stairs, elevation changes, and the climb back up out of the gorge.
* ✔️ Keep up with the group at a steady pace without needing frequent or extended stops.
* ✔️ Manage a full day of walking, travel, dinner, and evening sightseeing.

**This is not the event to use to test your fitness level or see how things go.** If you're unsure whether you can complete the hike, please choose an easier event instead.
If you find yourself unable to keep up, you may need to turn back or continue independently where the route and circumstances allow.

The group cannot stop or slow down significantly to accommodate someone who is struggling, as this affects the experience and schedule for everyone.
Please make an honest assessment of your abilities before committing. The goal is to keep the day safe, enjoyable, and on track for the entire group.

***

## 🍔 Dinner at Chuck's Roadhouse

After the hike, we'll head to **Chuck's Roadhouse on Clifton Hill** for a relaxed dinner. Everyone is responsible for the cost of their own meal.

⚠️ **Please note:** The restaurant has limited vegetarian options. If this means you won't be joining us for dinner, please let me know in advance so I can plan the numbers. Please don't leave this until the last minute, as I'll be arranging the dinner headcount.

***

## 🎇 Winter Festival of Lights

After dinner, we'll head down to the Falls to enjoy the **Niagara Falls Winter Festival of Lights**.
The surrounding area comes alive with illuminated displays and colourful seasonal installations. We'll take a relaxed evening stroll, enjoy the atmosphere, and stop for photos along the way.
Bring warm layers — temperatures near the Falls can drop, especially after dark! 🧣✨

***

## 💲 Meetup Fee

**$5 Meetup fee**
💵 Cash at the event, or
📧 E-transfer to **[mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)** before or on the day.

***

## 🚆 TRANSPORTATION REQUIREMENT — PLEASE READ

**Everyone must travel with the group on the GO Train to participate in this event.**
We will not meet people separately in Niagara Falls. Travelling together helps us coordinate the day's activities, stay on schedule, and avoid confusion about meeting points and transportation.
Please arrive on time at our Toronto meeting point. We will not be able to hold the train for late arrivals.

***

## 🕒 Travel Details (Approximate)

* **8:15 AM** — Meet outside the main doors of the Fairmont Royal York on Front Street West. Look for my Moose Hat! 🫎
* **8:30 AM** — Depart for the GO Train.
* **9:03 AM** — Planned GO Train departure for Niagara Falls.
* **11:25 AM** — Expected arrival in Niagara Falls.
* **12:30 PM** — Planned start of the Niagara Glen hike.
* **4:30 PM** — Dinner at Chuck's Roadhouse.
* **6:00 PM** — Head down to the Falls for the Winter Festival of Lights.
* **8:00–9:00 PM** — Target return-train window to Toronto.

🚆 These times are approximate and depend on the transit schedule and conditions on the day. I'll share any necessary updates closer to the event. Please check the current GO Transit schedule before purchasing your ticket.

***

## 🎟️ Tickets & What to Bring

Please purchase the **GO + WEGO Combo Ticket** in advance. The previously listed round-trip price was approximately $20, but please check the current price and service details before buying.
👉 **[Click here for the Niagara Parks GO + WEGO offer](https://www.gotransit.com/en/partners-and-promotions/go-train-to-niagara-on-weekends)**

Bring:

* 🥾 Sturdy walking shoes or hiking boots with good grip.
* 💧 Water and snacks.
* 🧥 Warm layers for the evening.
* 📸 A camera or charged phone.
* 🎒 Anything else you need for a full day outdoors.

***

## ⚠️ Important Notes

* This is a full, active day involving a train journey, a hike, dinner, and evening sightseeing.
* The event is open to everyone — singles, couples, and friends — provided they can manage the hike.
* Please RSVP only if you understand the physical requirements and can commit to the day's itinerary.
* You can RSVP ahead of time or show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule, but please remember that the train arrangements and group itinerary require punctuality.
* Sometimes things happen and I may need to cancel or change the plans. Please watch the event page for updates.

***

👤 **Organized by Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**.

**Come for the hike.**
**Stay for the lights.**
**Leave with a full day of adventure and new connections.** 🍁🎄

title: York Circle Lecture Series
location: Life Sciences Building
description:
Don’t miss out on the chance to hear from some of York’s leading faculty members on a wide range of fascinating topics at our next York Circle session. Connect with other alumni, gain valuable insights from our featured professors, and ask your own questions on important topics.
Date: Saturday, Nov. 14
Time: 9 a.m. – 1 p.m.
Location: Life Sciences Building, Keele Campus
Tickets: $5 includes coffee, light snacks and lunch.

Attendees will have the opportunity to choose one lecture from each session during the registration process.
First sessions – 10 a.m. 

Diagnostic and Prognostic Medical Devices: From research to real-world impact
Presented by Neda Salahandish, Assistant Professor, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Biomedical Engineering, Lassonde School of Engineering, and CEO, WearDOXX
Drawing on examples from her research, Dr. Salahandish will discuss the development of diagnostic and prognostic medical devices, including electrochemical biosensors, microfluidic point-of-care technologies, wearable devices, and AI-enabled health platforms.

AI at the Dentist’s Chair: Transforming periodontal disease detection with DePERIO
Presented by Ebrahim Ghafar-Zadeh, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Gum disease is one of the most common oral health conditions, yet early detection can be challenging and often depends on specialized clinical assessment. This talk will introduce DePERIO, an AI-enabled portable technology developed to support rapid and accessible assessment of periodontal health.

Second Sessions – 11:20 a.m.

Microchips Meet Mind: Tiny electronics that listen to, and heal, the brain
Presented by Hossein Kassiri, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Lassonde School of Engineering
Professor Hossein Kassiri will share how his lab will bring hospital-quality brain monitoring into a comfortable headband through a tiny, wireless devices that detects epileptic seizures and stops them before they spread. This innovation could one day restore sight to people with retinal diseases.

From Lab to Life: Multifunctional materials and systems that sense, adapt and perform
Presented by Garrett Melenka, Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Lassonde School of Engineering and Gerd Grau, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Lassonde School of Engineering
By combining expertise in composite materials and additive manufacturing with printed electronics and sensing systems, Professors Garrett Melenka and Gerd Grau have collaborated on a number of projects from multifunctional carbon fiber composites to wearable smart knee brace technology. These talks bring the two researchers together to discuss how multifunctional materials move from the lab bench to practical, real-world devices.

The Glen Major Forest is one of the most mature forests within the Durham Regional Forest network. The route follows the wide trails with a very good variety of scenic viewpoints. We will do a large loop enjoying the many rolling hills.

The pace will be moderate, taking breaks along the way. We can adjust as needed. The length of the hike is roughly 10-11 km in 3hrs or more.

Come out and enjoy the crisp fall air and take in some forest bathing.

**Note**

- Arrive on time! Cancel if you can't make it.
- Know your limits! Hike within your fitness level.
- Dress for the conditions.
- Proper footwear is required.
- Be aware and prepared for ticks.
- Free Parking.
- No Dogs.
- The hike will be canceled if the weather doesn't cooperate.

**We promptly leave at**
**9:37 am.**

Hope to see you there!

title: The Sororum Presents: A Step Through Time
location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON, M5S 1W7, Canada
description:
On Saturday, November 14th, join us in the heart of Yorkville as we step into a world of history, art, and craftsmanship. 




Our journey begins at the iconic Bata Shoe Museum, housed within Raymond Moriyama’s award-winning architectural landmark. Here, we’ll uncover fascinating stories of craftsmanship, culture, and human expression before enjoying a hands-on creative experience. 
From the museum, we’ll make our way to the historic Oxley for an intimate lunch and engaging conversation, bringing together the elements that make every Sororum gathering special: discovery, meaningful dialogue, and the joy of connecting with extraordinary women. 
How Our Day Will Unfold
10:30 AM – 12:15 PM | Private Guided Museum Tour 
We’ll begin with a private guided exploration of two remarkable exhibitions, each revealing how something as familiar as footwear can tell extraordinary stories about the people, cultures, and civilizations that came before us. 

Unearthing Vindolanda: Footwear from the Edge of the Roman Empire — Step back nearly 2,000 years and discover remarkably preserved footwear offering a rare and intimate glimpse into everyday life along the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.
Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World — Journey across cultures and generations to discover the beauty, symbolism, and extraordinary artistry of beadwork, and the stories of identity, tradition, and craftsmanship woven into every creation.

12:15 PM – 1:00 PM | A Hands-On Leatherworking Experience 
From appreciating craftsmanship to trying our hand at it! 
We’ll learn about traditional leatherworking techniques before creating our very own custom leather keychain — a beautiful little keepsake to remember the day. 
1:15 PM – 3:00 PM | Lunch & Guided Discussion at The Oxley 
At the heart of every Sororum gathering is the opportunity to connect, share perspectives, and enjoy thoughtful conversation. 
We’ll continue our afternoon at The Oxley, a charming British-inspired restaurant nestled within a late-19th-century Victorian townhouse in Yorkville. With its old-world character and inviting atmosphere, it provides a wonderful setting to gather around the table. 
Over a specially arranged prix fixe lunch, we’ll enjoy delicious food, warm company, and a guided discussion inspired by the stories and discoveries of our morning together. 
3:00 PM Onward | Discover Yorkville 
For those wishing to extend the day, Yorkville awaits! 
Enjoy an afternoon exploring one of Toronto’s most charming neighbourhoods, where historic Victorian streetscapes meet art galleries, inviting cafés, and beautiful boutiques. A lovely opportunity to linger, explore, and enjoy the autumn atmosphere at your own pace. 
Event Details & Pricing
Event Ticket: $75 per person 
Includes: 

Admission to the Bata Shoe Museum
Exclusive private guided museum tour
Hands-on leatherworking workshop and keepsake
Facilitated group discussion at The Oxley

Lunch: $40 per person + applicable taxes 
The Sororum has arranged a special prix fixe menu exclusively for our group. Lunch is paid individually by each guest at the restaurant and is not included in the event ticket. 
More Than an Outing. A Shared Experience.
At The Sororum, we believe the most memorable experiences are those that inspire curiosity, spark meaningful conversation, and bring women together. 
A Step Through Time is an invitation to discover something new, celebrate the artistry and stories of those who came before us, and create a few wonderful memories of our own. 
We look forward to sharing this special day with you.

title: 14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II
location: Meridian Arts Centre, 5040 Yonge St, North York, ON M2N 6R8, Canada
description:
14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II

14th SooRyu Dance Festival — Symbiosis II


The Korean Dance Studies Society of Canada (KDSSC) presents the 14th SooRyu Dance Festival — Symbiosis II, a two-day celebration bringing together artists from Korean, Indigenous, and diverse Canadian artistic traditions through dance, music, and cultural exchange.

Exploring how different cultures, bodies, and artistic voices connect through movement, Symbiosis II invites audiences to experience a range of traditional and contemporary performance practices.

Sunday, November 15 — Main Performance | 4 PM - Meridian Arts Centre Studio Theatre

Experience an afternoon of live performance featuring Mi Young Kim Dance Company, Culture & Arts Creative Research Institute J.D.C. (South Korea), U Dance Company (South Korea), William Lau, Mafa Thomas, Johnathan Morin, Hyang Ok Kim, Eun Ji Kim, and Hayun Jeong.

From Korean traditional performance to contemporary dance and diverse movement practices, the festival creates a space for artists and audiences to encounter different perspectives and discover connections through the performing arts.

Saturday, November 14 — Free Workshop Series - Meridian Arts Centre Upper Gallery

Discover different artistic traditions through a series of free workshops at the Meridian Arts Centre's Upper Gallery. Participants can explore Korean creative dance, K-Pop choreography, African rhythm and movement, beginner tap dance, Chinese Opera makeup, and Korean sangmo dance and janggu drumming.

These workshops offer an opportunity to learn from artists working across different cultural and movement traditions. Registration is required.


See our full festival schedule at www.koreandance.net http://www.koreandance.net

  * Dates: November 14–15, 2026
  * Venue: Meridian Arts Centre, 5040 Yonge Street, North York, ON
  * Main Performance: Sunday, November 15, at 4 PM
  * Tickets: Purchase tickets through Ticketmaster: www.ticketmaster.ca/event/1000654ECA552214 https://www.ticketmaster.ca/event/1000654ECA552214
  * Free Workshop Registration: Register through: forms.gle/jAEp1z5F27icwgj27 https://forms.gle/jAEp1z5F27icwgj27


Presented by the Korean Dance Studies Society of Canada (KDSSC), the SooRyu Dance Festival supports the presentation and exchange of Korean dance and other artistic traditions within Canada's diverse cultural landscape.

Join us in exploring the connections between cultures, traditions, and artistic voices through the universal language of movement.

title: The Battle of Lundy's Lane (LECTURE ON THE GO)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026-2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

The Battle of Lundy’s Lane was one of the largest and bloodiest battles fought during the War of 1812. It took place on July 25, 1814, near Niagara Falls. American forces had crossed into Upper Canada (Ontario) and were pushing north along the Niagara Peninsula. British troops, Canadian militia, and Indigenous allies moved to stop them, and the two armies met near a small country lane known as Lundy’s Lane.

The fierce battle lasted well into the night, with soldiers often fighting in darkness, and confusion.
One of the most important points in the battle was a hill where British artillery had been placed. Both sides recognized its importance and launched repeated attacks. It was incredibly intense, with troops charging, and retreating, again and again. Officers on both sides were wounded, and casualties mounted. By the time the battle ended, neither army had achieved a clear victory, but the Americans eventually withdrew from the area, leaving the British in control of the field. It was a costly struggle, and thousands were killed or missing.

Today, the Battle of Lundy’s Lane is remembered as a turning point in the Niagara campaign and one of the defining battles of the war. The battle demonstrated the determination of the Canadians who fought to defend this country.

Although the war itself ended without major territorial changes, Lundy’s Lane became an important symbol of resilience. Visitors can still explore the historic battlefield in Niagara Falls and learn about the dramatic events that unfolded there more than two centuries ago, and made the country we call Canada. If you like history and Canadian history at that, or want to learn so much more then this lecture is for you.

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

Celebrate the beauty of autumn through clay in this hands-on ceramic workshop. Participants will learn to create small mamezara (豆皿) — Japanese bean dishes — inspired by the natural shapes, textures, and colours of the season. You'll have the opportunity to make 2–3 small dishes, choosing from autumn-inspired designs such as leaves and tree bark. A practitioner of Chado (the Japanese Way of Tea) as well as Chinese tea, Helen’s love of tea deeply informs her creative practice. She specializes in ceramic wares for Japanese and Chinese tea rituals, everyday living, and multisensory food experiences in restaurants and cafés. Through her work, Helen hopes to bring people together through tea and handmade culture, creating memories, stories, and vessels that can be cherished and passed down for generations.

title: Aki no Tabi Workshop: Crafting Our Narratives with Erica H. Isomura and Nico Koyanagi
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Led by artist Erica H. Isomura and peer support worker Nico Koyanagi, this interactive workshop invites community members to reflect on their personal stories through writing prompts, dialogue, and a hands-on paper craft activity. Through group sharing, we hope to surface both shared and divergent community narratives — building deeper understanding and compassion for ourselves and one another. Participants will create a handmade "pocket altar" to take home: a small talisman to carry forward, encouraging continued reflection and intention-setting through the changing season ahead. Tickets Workshop from 1:30 PM to 4:00 PM JCCC Members: $10 Non-members: $20 Buy Tickets Nobody will be turned away for lack of funds. Please email Izumi at izumik@jccc.on.ca if the cost is a barrier. Artist Bios Erica H. Isomura is an artist, writer, and educator whose work is rooted in community. She was raised by a Chinese Canadian mom and sansei dad on the west coast beside the Sto:lo (Fraser River). Erica's inter- and multi-disciplinary practice combines storytelling, book arts, printmaking, collage and mixed-media art with land-based and critical diasporic knowledge. Erica has taught community art, bookmaking, and creative writing workshops across Canada. She holds an MFA in Creative Writing from the University of Guelph. Nico Koyanagi is a mixed-race yonsei, registered social worker, community organizer, educator, and mediator who prioritizes connection and healing in all aspects of her work. She grew up as a settler in Nogojiwanong on Michi Saagiig Nishnaabeg territory (Peterborough, ON). Through her community work with the BIPOC Growing Collective, Mata Ashita, and Tsuru for Solidarity, Nico is interested in how we can live with more compassion, kindness, and care towards ourselves, each other, and the earth alongside challenging oppression in all forms. Images 1: Photo by Kayla Isomura 2: Erica H. Isomura (left) and Nico Koyanagi (right)

title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto HISTORITOUR - LA JUNCTION - À la croisée des voies ferrées 2ème partie
location: Wallace Avenue Fotbridge, Toronto, ON, M6P 1X5, Canada
description:
Départ : À l’arrêt de bus Dundas St West & Glenlake Avenue (bus 40 A, 40 B et 140), à quelques pas du Wallace Footbridge.
Arrivée : Arrêt de tramway #505 ou #506 Sterling road and Dundas
Guides : Wafa Smiai – Rolande Smith 
Malgré son nom presque jumeau, Junction Triangle est un quartier distinct de The Junction : né lui aussi du même noeud ferroviaire, mais historiquement rattaché à la ville de West Toronto plutôt qu’à West Toronto Junction. Triangle formé par les voies ferrées du CN/CP à l’ouest, la ligne GO Barrie à l’est, et le faisceau ferroviaire du CP au nord, ce secteur reste aujourd’hui l’un des plus purs témoins du paysage industriel qui a fait naître tout le secteur — Junction comme Junction Triangle. 
Cette visite reste entièrement dans ce périmètre compact, et racontera une autre facette du même combat patrimonial : moins de bâtiments individuellement classés, mais un tissu industriel entier, et une question récurrente sur qui a le droit de continuer à l’occuper.

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: BOOK LAUNCH: STOP ANTIBLACK RACISM, by Nadia L. Hohn

📚🚀✊🏿Join award-winning author and educator Nadia L. Hohn for the launch of her latest release, STOP ANTIBLACK RACISM: 8 WAYS TO ACT NOW.
In this practical book, part of the Take Action Series by Orca Book Publishers, Hohn identifies 8 steps for everyone - Black and non-Black people - to combat anti-Black racism. Together the steps offer readers practical ways to overcome ignorance, take a stand, and get back up after experiencing racism. The book includes a glossary and a list of resources for further exploration of the topic.
Nadia is one of Toronto's favourite authors, bringing tremendous experience in education and publishing to her work - this is her 12th book! She not only writes but sings, plays the piano, draws - a true artivist! title: Paper Quilling: Holiday Ornament Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled workshop on paper quilling and learn how to make amazing art with paper strips!
Celebrate the cozy charm of November with a festive paper quilling workshop where you’ll create your very own handcrafted holiday ornament in your choice of colours and design. This relaxing, hands‑on session is perfect for beginners and craft lovers looking to welcome the winter season with something beautifully handmade.
 
With guided instruction and all materials provided, you’ll enjoy a peaceful creative break and leave with a finished ornament ready to hang.
 
All materials provided. Suitable for adults and children ages 10 and above.
 
Saturday, November 14, 2 to 4 p.m.
Public $50, TBG Members $45 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Du Symbolisme à l’Expressionnisme : le moi en question.
description:
En un temps où l’industrialisation est triomphante, certains peintres et écrivains sont, en cette fin du XIXe siècle, en proie à une inattendue inquiétude existentielle : le rationalisme explique-t-il à lui-seul le sens de la vie et de l’histoire ? Ces interrogations seront parfaitement résumées par le titre du tableau que Paul Gauguin exécute en 1898 :
D’où venons-nous ? Que sommes-nous ? Où allons-nous ?
De Van Gogh à George Grosz en passant par Edvard Munch, les peintres explorent alors dans leurs autoportraits ces champs d’inquiétude qui étreignent les consciences, en de fascinants tableaux hallucinés.
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

title: Toronto's Ravines: Nature and History at Your Doorstep
location: Richview, Room A, 2nd Floor
description:
Toronto's ravine landscapes are not just a sanctuary for wildlife; they also protect the city against flooding and allow us to enjoy nature at our doorsteps. This presentation by the Toronto Field Naturalists shares how the ravines are changing over time; how they are responding to numerous pressures and how you can explore and help protect them.
Presenter Bio:
Ellen Schwartzel is a former president of the Toronto Field Naturalists, and she enjoys leading walks through Toronto's ravines.  Ellen's career in environmental policy included 23 years with the Environmental Commissioner of Ontario. She was Ontario's Deputy Environmental Commissioner for four years, until retiring in 2018.  Ellen’s academic training was in Botany, and she received her BSc and MSc at the University of Toronto.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Beginner Knitting Course - November -  Saturdays
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a three session Beginner Knitting Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday November 14th, 21st and 28th from 2:30-4:00pm Have you always wanted to learn to knit? We’ve got you covered! Beginner Knitting is a course for brand new beginners, and over these three 1.5hr classes, Mike will teach you everything you need to create a basic project from beginning to end. Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. (No experience necessary) Materials: Yarn and needles will be provided. What We’ll Learn - How to make a slip knot. - Casting on. - The Knit stitch. - The Purl stitch. - Exploring Knit / Purl combinations. - Binding off. - Weaving in ends. - Fixing common mistakes and how to avoid them. - Common uses of flat knitting. - Intro into Ravelry. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! About the instructor : Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Classes cancelled less than 48 hrs prior to the start of the class will not be reimbursed.

title: The PATH System: Specialist Course and Guide! (FULL PATH TOUR)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

So many walkers have expressed interest in a full explanation of the dreaded PATH, so here it is. A full course on the PATH, its history and explanation. You will become a PATH specialist after this, guaranteed!

I've heard it so many times, with so many people, the common refrain, "I got lost in the PATH." If you are one of the many who have simply vanished in Toronto's underground never to be seen again, check out this popular historical walking tour.

This tour demystifies the PATH system and explains how it works in grand detail. It takes walkers through the system and points out the crucial connectors and branches within the system to effortlessly guide the lost through the maze. Once experienced the PATH will be an invaluable aid to navigating the downtown, in both summer and winter, rain or shine, hurricane or drought. You might even enjoy getting lost in the underground, lost but not forgotten.

This is the full PATH course curriculum:

Part 1: The History of THE PATH
Part2: Connectors and signboards
Part 3: Understanding the above ground connection
Part 4: Hidden paths to get one around quickly
Part 5: The Blind Spots and how to work with them
Part 6: The Maps
Part 7: Getting from here to there!

This walk is for all fitness levels and skills. This tour is indoors, so please dress for the conditions, and is considered an all-weather​ tour.

The walk begins **inside** the Atrium on Bay at the northeast corner of Dundas Street West and Bay Street adjacent to the Red Lobster restaurant!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

Group Instagram -
@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

title: Meet New People, Great Conversations & 50+ Board Games | 25–45 | Fast Friends
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Ever wish there were an easier way to turn a room full of strangers into people you actually want to talk to?
*That’s what Fast Friends is designed for.*

Instead of arriving at a busy pub and wondering who to approach, our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, giving you the chance to meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You get a little structure to make connecting easier — without making the evening feel forced or formal.

And once the hosted rounds finish, you can keep the evening going. 🎲
We’re back at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown — a relaxed Irish pub with food, drinks and 50+ board games, giving you plenty of ways to continue socialising with the people you’ve met.

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto14thnov.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto14thnov.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10
Regular: CAD $15
At the Door: CAD $20 cash — to host Kristabelle
Booking ahead helps us plan the right group size and venue space, and your ticket confirms your place.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Faye, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? Completely fine. Many guests arrive solo, and we’ll help you get comfortable and connected from the start.
7:30 PM — Fast Friends
This is where the evening gets going.
You’ll move through a series of short, guided conversations, meeting different people along the way. Our host keeps the rotations moving, so you don’t have to worry about who to approach or what to do next.
Just show up, join the conversation and see who you click with.

✨ Themed Connection Rounds
Throughout the evening, we’ll mix in themed rounds and interactive prompts designed to make connecting easier.
They’ll help you discover shared interests, experiences and unexpected things you have in common — taking the conversation beyond the usual small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — Board Games & Socialising
Once the hosted rounds finish, the evening doesn’t have to.
Stout has 50+ board games available, making it easy to keep the conversations going. Pick a game with the people you’ve met, grab another drink, join a group or simply continue chatting.
You don’t have to be a serious gamer — the games are simply another easy way to socialise and get to know people.

🍻 Staying Later?
Stout’s current After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 15–25 new people in one evening
✔️ Guided conversations make meeting people easier
✔️ Meet different people through rotating conversations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games available afterwards 🎲
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Most guests come solo
✔️ Plenty of time to keep socialising after the hosted rounds
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

👋 Who Is It For?
Ages 25–45
Whether you’ve just moved to Toronto, have lived here for years, or simply feel like your social circle could use some fresh faces, you’re welcome.
You don’t need to know anyone beforehand or arrive with a group.
Come by yourself, bring a friend, or simply come ready to have a few good conversations and see where the evening takes you.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come for the conversations. Stay for the games. Leave with new connections. ❤️

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

title: Meridian Arts Centre:  Canadian Golha Orchestra and Sepideh Raissadat
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
In this unforgettable concert, **the Canadian Golha Orchestra joins forces with acclaimed Persian music vocalist Sepideh Raissadat** to present rarely performed masterpieces of Iranian orchestral music. Timeless works by Rouhollah Khaleghi, Ali-Naqi Vaziri, Ali Tajvidi, and other pioneering composers will be brought to life through Raissadat’s velvety voice and the 40-piece orchestra’s expressive interpretation of these intricate and captivating melodies.

***INFO Link here--***

https://tolive.com/Event-Details-Page/reference/Canadian-Golha-Orchestra-2026?utm_medium=crosspromo&utm_source=partner&utm_campaign=canadiangolhaorchestra2026&utm_content=torontoisculture

Ticket link is below.

Inspired by the legacy of the *historic Golha radio orchestra*, the Canadian Golha Orchestra offers a refined interpretation of beloved repertoire by past masters, rooted in the Dastgāh tradition, alongside works by contemporary composers. Together, **the 40-piece orchestra** and Raissadat’s heartfelt artistry promise to immerse audiences in the profound beauty and emotional depth of Persian music.

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre, 1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

Directed by Bonnie Duff

Produced by Bonnie Duff and Miranda Wiseman

Featuring Lara Lucia as Bernadette and Jack Copland as Oliver

Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Nov 15 [Sundays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Description: 

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course.

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Sundays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesday)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🍁 Fall Walk: Glen Stewart Ravine & Beach Boardwalk Adventure! 🍦🌊
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
## 🍁 **Fall Walk: Glen Stewart Ravine & Beach Boardwalk Adventure!** 🍦🌊

Join us for a **beautiful fall walk** through one of Toronto’s most scenic spots — the **Glen Stewart Ravine** — followed by a stroll along the **Beach Boardwalk**!

We’ll take in the crisp autumn air, the colourful leaves, and the sound of the waves — plus a treat (or two) along the way.

Our walk begins at **Main Subway Station**, where we’ll make our way down **Main Street**, head east along **Kingston Road**, and then wander through the **Glen Stewart Ravine** — one of Toronto’s best hidden gems.
After exploring the ravine, we’ll stop for a well-deserved treat at **Ed’s Real Scoop**, home to some of the *best ice cream in the city*! 🍨
If you’re not in an ice cream mood, no worries — there’s a cozy coffee shop right across the street. ☕

From there, we’ll head down to the **Boardwalk**, walk along the lake, loop around **Ashbridges Bay** and finish our adventure at **Woodbine Beach**, taking in those gorgeous fall views of the water.

This is the perfect way to soak up the fall season before winter sneaks in! 🍂

**A Special Guest Joining Us!**

We're excited to welcome Miles Howard, visiting us from Boston on November 14–15!

Miles is writing *HIKE EVERY CITY*, a book (coming in 2028) exploring urban hiking, community, and how exploring cities on foot brings people together. He also runs a similar urban hiking project in Boston called *Walking City Trails*.

He'll be joining us for both weekend outings, including this walk, to experience our group firsthand and meet our members.

Feel free to say hello, share your experiences, and chat with Miles if you'd like. No pressure, of course!

It's exciting to see our community getting noticed beyond Toronto. Let's give Miles a warm welcome!

***

###

***

### 📍 **Meetup Details**

**Meeting Spot:** Outside **Main Subway Station** — I’ll be waiting and easy to spot in my **Moose Hat!** 🦌
**Meeting Time:** **11:30 A.M.** (I’ll wait about 5 minutes before we head out.)
**Ending Spot:** **Woodbine Beach**

***

### 💲 **Meetup Fee**

$5 (cash 💵 or e-transfer 📲 to **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**)
You can send it before or the day of the event!

***

### 🥾 **What to Bring**

* Water
* Comfortable walking shoes
* A snack or a few bucks for ice cream ☺️
* A cozy sweater — it might get breezy by the water!

###

***

### ⚠️ **A Quick Note**

Sometimes things come up and I might need to cancel or reschedule. Please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

***

### 👋 **About This Group**

This group is open to **everyone** — whether you’re single or not, new to Toronto, or just looking to be social and make friends!
We also host **movies, hikes, arts & culture events, and restaurant outings.**
You can RSVP ahead of time — or just show up the day of if you’re feeling spontaneous!

***

Beginner Knitting is a course for brand new beginners, and over these three 1.5hr classes, Mike will teach you everything you need to create a basic project from beginning to end. title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: The U of T, Yorkville and Rochdale College (MEGA-TOUR)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**This is a revised route for 2026 to take in the history of the historic Rochdale College!**

On March 15, 1827, a royal charter was issued by King George IV, for the establishment of King's College. The charter was the result of the efforts of John Strachan, the Anglican Bishop of Toronto, the College's first president.

King's College was a religious institution tied to the Church of England and the Family Compact. In 1849, the newly elected government of Canada voted to rename the College, University of Toronto and broke with the church. Strachan resigned to open Trinity College as a private seminary.

University College was created as a branch of University of Toronto. During the American Civil War, the threat of Union blockade prompted the creation of the University Rifle Corps, which saw action against the Fenians on the Niagara border in 1866.

Founded in 1830 by Joseph Bloor, and William Botsford Jarvis, the Village of Yorkville was muddy York's northern residential suburb.

With historic establishments like The Red Lion Inn, Yorkville Town Hall or even the fierce political radical William Lyon Mackenzie, it was here that notoriety was achieved, in Yorkville itself.

Omnibus horse drawn streetcar service started in 1849 to connect the old St. Lawrence Market in Toronto with Yorkville, and by 1853, the population of the village had reached 1,000 residents.

By the 1870s, Potter's Field, a cemetery stretching west of Yonge Street at Bloor Street was closed, and the remains moved to other area cemeteries. Yorkville was growing fast, and soon Toronto was ready to pull the neighbourhood into its orbit. On February 1, 1883, Yorkville's name changed officially. It was now known as St. Paul's Ward!

This walking tour is for all fitness levels and skills. Please dress for the weather. The extensive walking tour begins at the Queen's Park SUBWAY Station at the **southwest corner** of University Avenue and College Street adjacent to the Tim Horton's at the corner.

The walk ends at the site of Historic Rochdale College at Bloor and Huron!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: 14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II
location: Meridian Arts Centre, 5040 Yonge St, North York, ON M2N 6R8, Canada
description:
14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II

14th SooRyu Dance Festival — Symbiosis II


The Korean Dance Studies Society of Canada (KDSSC) presents the 14th SooRyu Dance Festival — Symbiosis II, a two-day celebration bringing together artists from Korean, Indigenous, and diverse Canadian artistic traditions through dance, music, and cultural exchange.

Exploring how different cultures, bodies, and artistic voices connect through movement, Symbiosis II invites audiences to experience a range of traditional and contemporary performance practices.

Sunday, November 15 — Main Performance | 4 PM - Meridian Arts Centre Studio Theatre

Experience an afternoon of live performance featuring Mi Young Kim Dance Company, Culture & Arts Creative Research Institute J.D.C. (South Korea), U Dance Company (South Korea), William Lau, Mafa Thomas, Johnathan Morin, Hyang Ok Kim, Eun Ji Kim, and Hayun Jeong.

From Korean traditional performance to contemporary dance and diverse movement practices, the festival creates a space for artists and audiences to encounter different perspectives and discover connections through the performing arts.

Saturday, November 14 — Free Workshop Series - Meridian Arts Centre Upper Gallery

Discover different artistic traditions through a series of free workshops at the Meridian Arts Centre's Upper Gallery. Participants can explore Korean creative dance, K-Pop choreography, African rhythm and movement, beginner tap dance, Chinese Opera makeup, and Korean sangmo dance and janggu drumming.

These workshops offer an opportunity to learn from artists working across different cultural and movement traditions. Registration is required.


See our full festival schedule at www.koreandance.net http://www.koreandance.net

  * Dates: November 14–15, 2026
  * Venue: Meridian Arts Centre, 5040 Yonge Street, North York, ON
  * Main Performance: Sunday, November 15, at 4 PM
  * Tickets: Purchase tickets through Ticketmaster: www.ticketmaster.ca/event/1000654ECA552214 https://www.ticketmaster.ca/event/1000654ECA552214
  * Free Workshop Registration: Register through: forms.gle/jAEp1z5F27icwgj27 https://forms.gle/jAEp1z5F27icwgj27


Presented by the Korean Dance Studies Society of Canada (KDSSC), the SooRyu Dance Festival supports the presentation and exchange of Korean dance and other artistic traditions within Canada's diverse cultural landscape.

Join us in exploring the connections between cultures, traditions, and artistic voices through the universal language of movement.

*** Accessibility ***

  * Wheelchair accessible (flat entrance, elevator inside)
  * Armless chairs
  * Accessible, all-gender washrooms
  * ASL interpretation (See Note)*
  * Masks required (provided if needed) except if communicating by ASL
  * We are also hoping to project the text of performances on-screen but this is still in progress

* Note: Performance-based ASL interpretation is extremely challenging and takes many hours of preparation. Normally an event like this requires 2 ASL interpreters with extensive performance-based experience.

  * Both interpreters are experienced working with (and are members of) local 2SLGBTQ+ communities.

Soul City Social Club (Toronto, Canada)
Good day everyone,

Join us for a fun and interactive Sunday night celebrating the incredible music of the 1980s! We’ll listen to great songs, share memories and opinions, and talk about the artists and music that helped define this awesome decade of music!
ㅤ
This is more than just listening to music — everyone is encouraged to participate! Whether you grew up with these songs or simply love discovering great music from the past, come spend an enjoyable evening with friends and fellow music lovers.

title: Afternoon Book Club

Join us on the following Monday afternoons to discuss books in a friendly and social atmosphere: September 14th, October 19th, November 9th, and December 14th.
This month we will be reading
Martyr!
by Kaveh Akbar.
Martyr!
is the 2024 debut novel by Iranian-American poet Kaveh Akbar. It is a
New York Times
bestseller and the paper's 2024 "Best Books of the Year So Far." It was a finalist for the 2024
Waterstones Debut Fiction Prize
and shortlisted for the
National Book Award for
Fiction.
The novel follows Cyrus Shams, a newly sober, queer, Iranian-American who becomes consumed with the idea of martyrdom. With the musculature of poetry and incandescent ideas, images, and humour, the novel is an inedible and haunted searching. Guided by the voices of lost artists, poets, and kings, Cyrus embarks on a search that leads him to a terminally ill painter living out her final days in the Brooklyn Museum.
Participants can borrow a copy of the book from the Woodside Square branch upon registration.

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: AI Snake Oil
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
November’s book is
AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference
by computer scientists Arvind Narayanan & Sayash Kapoor. Copies of the book are available in print,
eBook
&
eAudiobook
format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"Confused about AI and worried about what it means for your future and the future of the world? You're not alone. AI is everywhere—and few things are surrounded by so much hype, misinformation, and misunderstanding. In AI Snake Oil, computer scientists Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor cut through the confusion to give you an essential understanding of how AI works, why it often doesn't, where it might be useful or harmful, and when you should suspect that companies are using AI hype to sell AI snake oil—products that don't work, and probably never will. While acknowledging the potential of some AI, such as ChatGPT, AI Snake Oil uncovers rampant misleading claims about the capabilities of AI and describes the serious harms AI is already causing in how it's being built, marketed, and used in areas such as education, medicine, hiring, banking, insurance, and criminal justice. The book explains the crucial differences between types of AI, why organizations are falling for AI snake oil, why AI can't fix social media, why AI isn't an existential risk, and why we should be far more worried about what people will do with AI than about anything AI will do on its own. The book also warns of the dangers of a world where AI continues to be controlled by largely unaccountable big tech companies. By revealing AI's limits and real risks, AI Snake Oil will help you make better decisions about whether and how to use AI at work and home."
In addition, we will be discussing Chapter 1 of
Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
by artificial intelligence and media researcher Kate Crawford.
Drop in. No registration required.

title: David Radice (Penn State University)
description:
Title: The Fate of Neutron Star Mergers

Abstract: In this talk, I will discuss the outcome of binary neutron star mergers and its consequences for their multi-messenger emission and nucleosynthesis yields. At one extreme, neutron star mergers can undergo prompt collapse to a black hole, which produces only faint electromagnetic emission. The threshold mass for this to occur is sensitive to how compressible matter is at the highest densities. Lower-mass systems can produce short or long-lived remnants, which evolve due to the presence of hydrodynamic and magnetohydrodynamic instabilities. I will argue that these mergers are accompanied by the ejection of substantial amount of material and can explain the kilonova seen in AT2017gfo. I will also discuss what postmerger gravitational waves can tell us about thermal effects and QCD phase transitions, and how the size of the disk may decide whether a merger produces a short or a long gamma-ray burst.

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 1
location: S. Walter Stewart, Meeting Room
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology .  On November 4th, 2026, it would be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Egyptology Specialist Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the moment of its discovery.  Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will recount the story leading to the discovery of the tomb and explore the remarkable objects found in its two chambers during the initial excavation.
