title: The Connection-Oriented Leader ft. Jody Wilson-Raybould and Roshan Danesh
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Spend an evening rethinking what leadership looks like when it's built on connection instead of hierarchy.
Make the most of your Connect IRL experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Try out tonight's
Conversation Station: The Common Ground
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger around the topic of staying in relationship across difference.
Join us at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon for
The Inbetween Leader
, with Indigenous leader and former justice minister of Canada Jody Wilson-Raybould, alongside internationally-renowned lawyer and peace-building educator Roshan Danesh.
Together, we'll take apart the assumption that unity requires sameness, examine what it means to stay connected to people you don't always agree with, and talk about why so many of our leadership models are actually failing our need for connection. Expect to leave with a clearer sense of what it looks like to hold a room — or a workplace, or a community — together without flattening what makes it diverse. What does connection actually require of a leader, beyond charisma or authority? How do Indigenous governance traditions offer a different model for staying in relationship through disagreement? And in a culture that treats leadership as something you perform from the top, what would it mean to reclaim it as something built collaboratively, in the in-between spaces of everyday interaction? Wilson-Raybould and Danesh, drawing on Indigenous governance traditions and integrative worldviews in
The Inbetween Leader: Cultivating Courage and Unity in a Complex World
, offer an alternative to competition-based leadership models — one that fosters interconnectedness, empowers diverse teams, and maintains unity without erasing difference. Building on their national bestsellers
True Reconciliation
and
Reconciling History
, they show how leaders in workplaces, communities, and families can create environments where everyone feels valued and genuinely connected. Come for a thoughtful conversation about the relationships that make real leadership possible.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jody Wilson-Raybould
Roshan Danesh
Farah Nasser
Read more:
The Inbetween Leader
Indian in the Cabinet
Reconciling History
***
Conversation Station | 6:00–7:00 pm & 8–9 pm
The Common Ground
A conversation station exploring the relationships that keep us connected even when we disagree: When has staying in a relationship with someone been harder than walking away — and what made it worth it? Who has shown you what it looks like to lead with humility? What's one thing you wish more people understood about connecting across difference? This station invites you to swap stories with the strangers next to you about the everyday work of staying together.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**

title: ECE Lecture Series: Professor Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani
location: Galbraith Building, Room 202 (GB202), 35 St George, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 1A4, Canada
description:
Anomaly Detection for Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: Tractable Algorithms with Probabilistic Guarantees
Join ECE for a guest lecture by Professor Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani, Associate Professor at the University of Toronto. 
Abstract
In this seminar, we study a broad class of anomaly/fault detection for large-scale nonlinear dynamical systems. Noting a connection between the diagnosis filter and the so-called behavioral sets of dynamical systems, we leverage tools from traditional model-based approaches and modern data-driven analytics to address the inherent complexity of the problem. We also discuss probabilistic guarantees for the proposed design. The discussion will be motivated by applications in power system security, autonomous vehicles, and leakage detection in water distribution networks. 
Biography
Professor Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani is an Associate Professor at the University of Toronto, where he joined in 2025. Prior to that, he was a faculty member at Delft University of Technology, having joined in 2016 following several research appointments at EPFL, ETH Zurich, and MIT between 2014 and 2016. He received the PhD degree from ETH Zurich, Switzerland, and the MSc and BSc degrees from Sharif University of Technology, Iran. His research interests include theoretical and practical aspects of decision-making problems in uncertain and dynamic environments, with applications in engineering systems and management. 
He currently serves as an associate editor of Operations Research, Transactions on Automatic Control, Mathematical Programming, Mathematics of Operations Research, and Open Journal of Mathematical Optimization. He was one of the three finalists for the Young Researcher Prize in Continuous Optimization awarded by the Mathematical Optimization Society in 2016, and a recipient of the 2016 George S. Axelby Outstanding Paper Award from the IEEE Control Systems Society. He received the ERC Starting Grant and the INFORMS Frederick W. Lanchester Prize in 2020. He is the recipient of the 2022 European Control Award.

title: Modern Careers: Unlocking New AI Career Paths
description:
Join one of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence,  Sangeetha Dikshit and guest speaker Bhumika Arora for this interactive discussion.
Artificial intelligence is changing more than just how software gets built. It is creating brand new ways to work across every industry. title: Seniors Club - Birds in Winter
location: Cliffcrest
description:
Cliffcrest invites all to our Seniors Club! Hang out and enjoy games, engaging presentations and workshops on a variety of topics.
This Month: Birds in Winter
Winter is a harsh season, yet many birds stay in Toronto and survive. Why don’t they all fly south? How do they stay warm and find food and shelter? Which birds stay and which ones migrate? Learn about migrant birds and their incredible journeys, visiting birds who come to the city from their boreal and Arctic homes, and our resident birds who spend the long, cold winter months here.
Join Monika Croydon, avid local birder and member of the Toronto Ornithological Club, to find out how we can all help birds in winter, from providing feeders and creating bird-friendly gardens and homes, to supporting conservation and research as Citizen Scientists.

Presenter Bio:
Ellen Schwartzel is a former president of the Toronto Field Naturalists, and she enjoys leading walks through Toronto's ravines.  Ellen's career in environmental policy included 23 years with the Environmental Commissioner of Ontario. She was Ontario's Deputy Environmental Commissioner for four years, until retiring in 2018.  Ellen’s academic training was in Botany, and she received her BSc and MSc at the University of Toronto.

title: Book Launch: Lisa Hanawalt's I Can't Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex
location: Lillian H. Smith
description:
Join
Lisa Hanawalt
in conversation with
Ann Fitzpatrick
as she launches
I Can’t Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex.
I Can’t Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex
marks Hanawalt’s long-awaited return to comics. In this brutally honest, vulnerable yet still irreverently funny memoir, a horse girl now in her forties  reflects back on a lifetime of obsessions and confronts the many hurdles of a life fully lived.
From confronting whether or not to have kids, to being an anxious lil’ freak, to caring for a sick horse, to dealing with a major breakup and the ensuing lustfulness—Hanawalt delivers a reading experience that’s relatable, affirming, and absolutely hilarious.
Lisa Hanawalt
is an artist and writer living in Los Angeles, CA. She is the creator of the animated series
Tuca & Bertie
and the production designer/producer on
BoJack Horseman
and
Long Story Short
. Lisa has published four books with Drawn & Quarterly: M
y Dirty Dumb Eyes, Hot Dog Taste Test, Coyote Doggirl,
and
I Want You
. Her fifth book,
I Can't Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex
has already garnered rave reviews from
NPR, LitHub, Vulture
and
Publishers Weekly.
Anna Fitzpatrick
is the author of the novel
Good Girl
(Flying Books) and the picture book
Margot and the Moon Landing
(Annick Press). She was a full-time writer until Toronto rent prices forced her to get a day job, and now she works at a nonprofit that advocates for affordable housing.
Advance praise for
I Can’t Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex
“Lisa Hanawalt draws and writes the things we all wish we could say: about love, loss, and what it feels like to be in a human body."—Lena Dunham
"I can't stop thinking about how this is the best and funniest and most vulnerable book about being a horny girl who loves both horses and Kevin Costner that I have ever read."—Samantha Irby
“I couldn’t put this book down! I read it in one night which felt like a sleepover with a tender, bold, hilarious friend who knew everything about me; nothing was shameful when we were together.”—Miranda July
"Ironies of life: Here she’s all obsessed with horses and riding horses, and she has this big ass, which she openly admits to and draws...and here I am obsessed with women with big asses and wanting to jump on them and ride them like horses. I guess I should write back to Lisa and ask her if she’d give me a ride on her big ass. She’d probably say no. Ironies of life."—R. Crumb.
Books will be available for purchase with the Beguiling book store.

description:
The WoodGreen Foundation’s Young Leaders Council (YLC) https://www.woodgreen.org/about-the-foundation will host its annual Cocktails for a Cause fundraiser on November 17, 2026, at the Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO), bringing together Toronto’s young professionals and community leaders for an evening dedicated to raising awareness and support of WoodGreen’s new Youth Wellness Centre.

WoodGreen Foundation’s YLC brings together emerging philanthropists and community-minded professionals committed to addressing some of Toronto’s most pressing social challenges. Through fundraising, community engagement and education, YLC members mobilize their networks to advance WoodGreen’s mandate and create meaningful local impact.

Guests will enjoy an engaging evening connecting with Toronto’s young professionals, community leaders and changemakers over cocktails and a curated culinary experience. The event will feature a fireside chat with distinguished leaders from the world of sports, including 2026 Winter Olympics bronze medallist and five-time Canadian national champion ice dancer Piper Gilles https://olympic.ca/team-canada/piper-gilles/ , and Lisa Ferkul https://www.linkedin.com/in/lisaferkul/ , Chief Revenue Officer of the Toronto Tempo https://tempo.wnba.com/ .

Guests will also receive exclusive access to an exhibit at the AGO, alongside a silent auction and a lucky draw featuring prizes donated by local businesses - all in support of WoodGreen’s one-stop social services hub for youth.

WoodGreen’s Youth Wellness Centre https://www.woodgreen.org/programs/youth-wellness-centre provides young people aged 12–29 a full range of free services, including settlement support, housing, employment, education, financial assistance and cultural programming. The Centre also offers free wellness workshops and skill-building opportunities to help young people access resources and build skills for the future.

“Cocktails for a Cause is an opportunity for Toronto’s next generation of leaders to turn their passion for community into meaningful action,” said Olivia Clark https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivia-clark-a22193125/ , Chair of WoodGreen’s YLC. “We look forward to bringing people together at the iconic AGO to support the essential wrap-around services WoodGreen offers young people as they navigate important stages of their lives.”

You’ll discover what happens when you combine security and compliance requirements with the need for speed and innovation — and why this is where the most interesting technology careers are headed. Walk away understanding the real-world challenges that drive enterprise strategy, and how the problems being solved today are defining the future of cloud technology. 
Following Ernani’s session, you’ll have the opportunity to dive deeper during a hands-on workshop led by cloud technologists, learning directly from industry leaders and applying the concepts in real-time.

Through real-world examples, you’ll explore the trade-offs between governance, cost optimization, resilience, and developer experience — and discover why enterprise cloud infrastructure is at the forefront of industry innovation. Learn the decision-making frameworks that separate theoretical best practices from production reality and understand how the problems being solved today are defining the future of cloud technology.

Led by RBC cloud technologists, you’ll work through the decision-making frameworks that shape enterprise cloud strategy in highly regulated environments.

title: Civic Meetup #569: Happy town: Why scaling community is not like scaling a product
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom
description:
Topic: Happy town: Why scaling community is not like scaling a product

What does it take to build a less lonely city? Can we scale human connection the same way we scale a tech startup?

Happy Town began as a grassroots experiment in creating spaces where strangers could become friends. Through recurring walks, shared meals and community gatherings, it has grown into an evolving network hosts creating opportunities for more satisfying connections across Toronto.

But growing a community comes with distinct challenges not faced by companies or start ups.

What happens when growth creates pressure on the very relationships we’re trying to nurture? What if the most sustainable way to scale community isn’t to build a better product, but to build a movement?

Drawing on the experience of building Happy Town and its evolution into Less Lonely Winter, a collective effort to bring 25+ free community events per week to Toronto throughout winter, this talk explores our approach to community building. One rooted in the idea that nobody owns community; and the belief that connection is grown, not found.

‎

Speaker: Adam Chen (in-person)

Adam Chen works in mental health communications by day at HF Care, and grows community by night with Happy Town. He is a storytelling and live journalism performer, producer and director who dabbles in app development, having co-created the private-blogging app “Smaller World." Website

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

title: When The Dead Are Kept From Us
location: Online, online
description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. How do we honor our dead when they are kept from us? What happens to us when we are denied our chance to mourn? Let's come together to learn about and practice building ritual for grief when we are othered. Colleen (ʻoia/they/them) of Death Doula Does will guide participants through practical skills for honoring our mourning and grief in rituals when we have no body to hold. Colleen is a Kanaka Maoli, Queer, mutual aider, community-oriented death doula. Supporting those dying, caregivers for the dying, and grievers for over a decade, their work focuses on art-based grief spaces, queer end-of-life planning, and teaching how to be with death. title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

title: 2026 Duende International Flamenco Festival: Masterclasses
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
This special series of masterclasses offers dancers a rare opportunity to learn with three extraordinary flamenco artists, Óscar de los Reyes, Carmen Talegona, and El Yiyo.

Each workshop offers participants a deeper understanding of the art form’s power, precision, musicality, and emotional truth. The three artists brings a distinct voice, lineage, and approach, guiding dancers toward greater technical clarity, expressive range, and connection to rhythm, structure, and cante. Together, these masterclasses create a rich encounter with flamenco as a living, evolving art form — one that honours tradition while continuing to move boldly into the future.

Open to intermediate, advanced, and professional-level dancers, the workshops offer an inspiring environment for growth, exchange, and artistic discovery.

title: Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World
location: Aga Khan Museum, Massey Hall, Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium
description:
Celebrate flamenco’s global transformation through cross-cultural exchange at the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World.

From November 18 to 22, experience the vibrant evolution of flamenco — from its regional roots in Andalusia to a dynamic global art form shaped by cross-cultural exchange. This year’s lineup spans both traditional flamenco from Andalusia and innovative collaborations at the crossroads of qawwali and Persian muqam, tracing the art form’s evolution from its regional roots to a global practice.

title: Entrepreneurship 101
location: Live on Zoom @ Zoom
description:
Join us for an introductory workshop on entrepreneurship designed specifically for graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. This session will introduce practical frameworks for translating research, technical expertise, and emerging ideas into potential innovations for real-world solutions.
Participants will learn about the entrepreneurial journey, explore the steps involved in moving from research to application, and discover resources available to support them along the way. No prior business experience or fully developed idea is required.
By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to:

Understand the foundational concepts of innovation and entrepreneurship and how they apply within a research context.
Identify opportunities to translate research findings, specialized knowledge, or technical expertise into practical solutions.
Apply introductory frameworks to assess a problem, explore potential users, and develop an early-stage idea.
Understand the key stages involved in moving from research or academic study toward innovation, commercialization, or venture creation.
Develop a more entrepreneurial mindset by approaching uncertainty through experimentation, iteration, and continuous learning.
Build confidence in communicating ideas, testing assumptions, and taking the first steps toward launching an initiative.
Identify relevant programs, tools, mentors, funding opportunities, and institutional resources that can support their journey.

description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Bridging Minds: Supporting Mental Health in the Early Years (0–5) — Small Actions, Big Impact
description:
Dr. Aliza Israel and Dr. Tatiana Valverde, child psychiatrists at Women’s College Hospital, will explore why the early years of life are so important for children's mental health, emotional well-being, and development. From birth to age five, children begin to develop the foundations for relationships, emotional regulation, learning, and resilience. Through everyday interactions, play, and nurturing relationships, parents, caregivers, and communities can help create a strong foundation for lifelong well-being.
What to Expect:
Understanding Early      Childhood:
Why the first five years are an important period for brain      development, emotional growth, and lifelong mental health
The Power of      Relationships:
How responsive caregiving, secure relationships,      play, and everyday interactions help young children feel safe, connected,      and supported
Supporting Big      Feelings:
Understanding co-regulation and how parents and caregivers can help      young children navigate big emotions, manage frustration, and gradually      develop their own emotional regulation skills
Small Actions,      Lasting Impact:
Practical, everyday ways families, caregivers,      and communities can support children's mental health and help give every      child a healthy start
About the Presenters:
Dr. Aliza Israel is a child and adolescent psychiatrist at Women's College Hospital, and lecturer at the University of Toronto in child psychiatry and women's mental health. Her work focuses on the interplay between maternal and child mental health, and in promoting resilience in young families. Dr. Israel lives in Toronto, Canada, with her husband and three rapidly-growing boys.  She is also an amateur juggler who may or may not secretly wish to run away with the circus.
Dr. Tatiana Valverde da Conceicao is a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist at the Reproductive Life Stages Program at Women’s College Hospital. She’s an Assistant Professor at University of Toronto. Her clinical work involves general Child and Adolescent Psychiatry with a special focus on Early Childhood Mental Health.  In addition to her clinical and academic work, the experience of being a mother influences and enriches her professional perspective.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:
https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 2
location: North York Central Library, Auditorium (2nd floor)
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology. On November 4th, 2026, it will be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Egyptologist Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the time of its discovery. Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will conclude the story of the discovery and explore the remarkable objects found in the burial chamber and the treasury during the excavation of 1923.
Registration is encouraged but not required.

location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging workshop where you’ll learn about biodiversity, native plants and how to enhance your garden!
While other sessions in the Native Plant Series explore how to grow native plants from seed, this session focuses on choosing the right plants for your garden and finding the best place to plant them. The right plant in the right place is key to growing a successful garden. Whether your space is sunny or shady, dry or exposed to road salt, there are native plants suited to every condition.
 
We’ll also share local sources for native plants, shrubs and trees. Fall is the perfect time to plan additions to your garden for next year, so come learn how to make the best choices for your space!
 
Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 to 8 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.

title: Rachel Cusk: Life of M
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Critically acclaimed author Rachel Cusk shares her irresistible new novel.
Life of M introduces us to movie star M, one of the most recognizable faces of our time, whose image has been ubiquitous since she was a child.
With such fame, her life has the appearance of freedom: people are instantly obliging, spaces are altered to accommodate her, time can be rearranged. M may live in the same places as real people. She may meet her friends or collect her children from school or walk her dogs as they do. But it seems the rules of reality have melted away.
Now, a writer has decided to pay close attention to M’s life in the hope of understanding who she really is. It is hard not to feel ugly next to M, hard not to feel insignificant. But what truths―about the very experience of living―might this proximity allow the writer to briefly capture?
Rachel Cusk speaks with Sheila Heti about Life of M, an astonishing new novel about fame, power, beauty, and truth
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Rachel Cusk

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Farruquito: A Flamenco Dynasty
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Part of the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World, join us for a film screening that celebrates the legacy of Farruquito, one of the greatest flamenco dancers of this century.

Farruquito is celebrated as the finest flamenco dancer of his generation. He belongs to a legendary dynasty of bailaores (dancers). At only 20, he was already at the height of his success, captivating audiences around the globe from New York to Tokyo – with his extraordinary talent, yet the shadows of his family’s tumultuous history loomed large.

The film follows Farruquito’s journey through triumph and tragedy, focusing on a pivotal moment that changes everything — a tragic accident that leads to the death of a pedestrian and lands him in prison. This harrowing experience forces him to confront the demons of his past and the heavy burden of his family’s legacy.

description:
Join us for an introduction to Sleep Qigong & Self-Acupressure!
Sleep issues can occur at different times during our lives in a variety of ways and for different reasons. You might have trouble falling asleep; perhaps you can fall asleep easily but wake up several times throughout the night; you might fall asleep but wake up too early feeling you haven’t slept quite enough; or you suffer from insomnia. Stress, anxiety, depression, age, worry, and other factors can all contribute to sleep complications.
 
In this session, I will demonstrate and guide you through some holistic and non-invasive ways to deal with sleep issues. They will include simple self-acupressure, gentle qigong, helpful tips, and calming breathing exercises.
 
Whether you experience occasional or chronic sleep problems, this session can provide you with some alternative ways to deal with it.
Thursday, November 19, 10 to 11:30 a.m.

About David Leopold
Sifu David Leopold has been practicing, studying, researching and teaching martial and healing arts since 1994.
 
In 1999, Sifu David achieved his black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu. Since 1999, Sifu David has received numerous certifications in Tachi and weapon forms, and seven Qigong routines. In 2009, Sifu David received his Usui Reiki master certification from the Naturopathic School of Medicine in Toronto.
 
In 2012, Sifu David travelled to China to compete in the International Wushi Competition in Shanghai. He brought home 2 gold and a bronze medal.
 
By combining all these modalities and experiences, Sifu David brings a unique style of teaching that includes technique, philosophy, and practicality. Sify David’s approach to teaching is relaxed and he believes Taichi and Qigong practice should be useful in everyday life and enjoyable to do.
 
Sifu David has a passion for martial and healing arts. His holistic approach to wellness includes physical, emotional, spiritual and nutritional well-being. Sifu David continues to improve his skills as a practitioner, teacher/ mentor, and hopes to teach for the rest of his life.
 
Sifu David’s words of wisdom:
 
“To be a master of what you do, you must first be a master unto yourself.”

title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Leslie Kaelbling, “The Role of Rationality in Modern Robotics”
location: Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5G0G6, Canada
description:
This seminar is co-hosted with the Department of Computer Science 
Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, West Winter Garden (10th Floor) 
Register for the seminar 



The Role of Rationality in Modern Robotics
Abstract
The classical approach to AI designed systems that were rational at run-time: they had explicit representations of beliefs, goals, and plans and ran inference algorithms, online, to select actions. The rational approach was criticized (by the behaviorists) and modified (by the probabilists) but persisted in some form. More recently, relatively unstructured data-driven end-to-end approaches have demonstrated great success in a wide variety of domains, and began to seem like a plausible route to general-purpose intelligent robots. However, most recently, we have begun to see the limits of pure behavior learning and many practitioners are re-integrating forms of search and explicit reasoning into their approaches. 
Professor Kaelbling will revisit the rational-agent approach to the design of intelligent robots, from the perspectives of engineering effort, computational efficiency, cognitive modeling and understandability. They will present some current research focused on understanding the roles of learning in runtime-rational agents with the ultimate aim of constructing general-purpose human-level intelligent robots. 
Register for the seminar 
About Leslie Kaelbling
Leslie Pack Kaelbling is a Professor at MIT. She has an undergraduate degree in Philosophy and a PhD in Computer Science from Stanford, and was previously on the faculty at Brown University. She was the founding editor-in-chief of the Journal of Machine Learning Research. Her research agenda is to make intelligent robots using methods including learning, planning, and reasoning about uncertainty. She was doing agentic AI way before it was cool.

title: Nov 19 - Visualizing and Debugging Hugging Face's LeRobot Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop is a hands-on tour of what actually breaks when you load real LeRobot datasets, and how Voxel51's native LeRobot support in FiftyOne catches it.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 19, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/lerobot-workshop-november-19-2026)**

Robot learning data doesn't look like the data that trains most vision-language models. It's temporal, low-dimensional in the parts that matter most, embodiment-specific, and expensive to collect, and increasingly, it's shipped in Hugging Face's LeRobot format. But packaging robot data consistently isn't the same as being able to see it: episodes hide broken metadata, silently dropped sensor modalities, and mismatched schemas between robots that look identical on paper.

Starting from the core differences that make robot data hard (temporal structure, proprioception, action grounding, embodiment heterogeneity, data scarcity), we'll move into live debugging: a metadata bug that broke multiple dataset imports, sensor streams that vanish without an error, and two robots running an identical benchmark whose data is structurally incompatible. By the end, you'll know what to check before you trust a LeRobot dataset, and how to actually look inside one.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: Tubman Talks with Marie Laure Belomo Onguene: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
location: (3rd flr York Lanes, Rm 314)
description:
Tubman Talks with Marie Laure Belomo Onguene: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
Date: Thursday, November 19, 2026
Time: 2:30pm – 4:00pm EST
Location: Zoom
Register Here: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/K-bk-9K5Qm-JZMX3T3pK8g
Title: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
Abstract
The focus of the study is how mobile money moderates the effect of peak technology on gender economic inclusion in Africa, with thresholds of mobile money at which the effect
of peak technology on gender economic inclusion is mitigated, as well as evidence of positive synergies between digital finance and frontier technologies. Using a panel dataset of 31 African countries over the period 2010-2023, and drawing on fixed-effects models, Driscoll–Kraay robust estimations, Lewbel (2012) instrumental variable approaches, and quantile regressions, the study produces the following key findings. First, the baseline linear estimates indicate that frontier technology readiness (FRTI) is, on average, positively and significantly associated with the share of women in the labor force. Second, interactive and instrumental variable specifications reveal a fundamental structural heterogeneity: when mobile money and digital payment services are absent, the marginal effect of FRTI on women’s economic inclusion turns negative or insignificant. Third, threshold analysis identifies specific levels of financial digitalization beyond which the adverse effect of frontier technologies is fully mitigated or reversed into a positive synergy. These thresholds vary across specifications (ranging from approximately 0.53 to 1.65 on the digital finance scales) but consistently confirm a non-linear complementarity between technological capability and digital financial inclusion. Fourth, quantile regression results establish that the inclusive effect of technology is most pronounced at the upper end of the distribution of female labor force participation. Policy implications are discussed.
Bio
Marie Laure BELOMO ONGUENE is a lecturer in the Faculty of Economics and Management at the University of Yaoundé 2 Soa. She holds a Ph.D. from the University of Dschang in Cameroon and served as a postdoctoral researcher in the Open AIR program at the Center for Law, Technology, and Society at the University of Ottawa. In addition, she serves as a visiting researcher in the Department of Economics at York University in Canada under the supervision of Pralewa Yinka Olawoye. Between May 2023 and August 2023, she received a research mobility grant from the Observatory of the Economic Francophonie at the University of Lomé in Togo. Her research focuses on the socioeconomic challenges that emigration poses to migrants’ countries of origin. She is particularly interested in economic complexity, women’s political empowerment, and food security.

title: UNESCO World Philosophy Day (Laurie Paul, Yale University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building 100
description:
This year, we welcome as 2026 UNESCO World Philosophy Day lecture speaker Laurie Paul, the Millstone Family Professor of Philosophy and Cognitive Science Yale University. She explores relationships between the nature of the self, transformative experience, preference change, subjective value, temporal experience, causation, time, and perception. 
Talk Title
The paradox of transformation 
Talk Abstract
Transformative changes happen. They can be chosen or unchosen, wanted or unwanted, good or bad. They can occur as part of ordinary life transitions, as when one graduates from college, becomes a parent, marries, emigrates, or divorces, and they can occur in extraordinary circumstances, such as when one experiences a war, a serious physical accident, an invasive neurosurgical procedure, or cognitive change due to Alzheimer’s. I will develop a conceptual framework that characterizes the profound and paradoxical nature of the epistemic and personal transformation that transformative experience can bring, and explore some of the formal implications for models of decision and change.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: Nuclear Industry Panel Night - OPTIONS Program
description:
Thursday, November 19 | 5:00 – 7:00 PM | GB202 (Galbraith Building, 35 St. George St., Room 202) | Register in Advance* 
*PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS EVENT IS AVAILABLE EXCLUSIVELY TO UOFT ENGINEERING GRADUATE STUDENTS. 
Explore the cutting edge of nuclear innovation and the need for talent in this rapidly evolving field. This special evening brings together industry leaders and academic voices to spotlight opportunities, challenges, and the future of the nuclear workforce development.  
ISTEP is proud to bring you this event with the support of our departmental co-sponsors: 

Department of Chemical Engineering & Applied Chemistry
Department of Civil & Mineral Engineering
The Edward S. Rogers Sr. Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering
Department of Mechanical & Industrial Engineering

Featured Speakers:  
Sean Granville, Board of Directors, NWMO | Former COO and Chief Nuclear Officer, OPG | President of BNKA Consulting Inc. 
As former Chief Operations Officer and Chief Nuclear Officer of Ontario Power Generation (OPG), Sean Granville was responsible for all of OPG’s generating fleet, with a capacity of over 15,400 megawatts of electricity. This consisted of 10 nuclear units, 66 hydro stations, two thermal stations, one solar facility, as well as oversight of OPG subsidiaries Atura Power and Eagle Creek Renewable Energy. Mr. Granville’s nuclear career spans 39 years including three years at Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station in New Brunswick. Mr. Granville’s energy industry experience includes a World Association of Nuclear Operators secondment, as well as membership in the Canadian Nuclear Association and the CANDU Owners Group. Mr. Granville is also a board member of Women in Nuclear and past chair of the Canadian Chief Nuclear Officer Forum, as well as a past member of the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations Executive Advisory Group. Mr. Granville is currently providing executive consulting services to the energy industry. Mr. Granville is a graduate of the University of Waterloo with a Bachelor of Applied Science in Mechanical Engineering.  
Laurie Swami, President and CEO of Nuclear Waste Management Organization  
Ms. Laurie Swami is the President and CEO of the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO). She was appointed to the role in 2016 and is responsible for implementing Canada’s plan for the long- term management of used nuclear fuel.   
Prior to joining the NWMO, Ms. Swami spent 30 years, primarily in nuclear operations, at Ontario Power Generation. She served as Senior Vice-President of Decommissioning and Nuclear Waste Management, overseeing the operation of nuclear waste management facilities and planning for the decommissioning of a nuclear generating facility.   
Ms. Swami has extensive experience leading Environmental Assessment projects, including nuclear refurbishments. She has appeared before Joint Panel Reviews (CEA and CNSC) for the Darlington New Nuclear Project and OPG’s Deep Geologic Repository Project. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Engineering Chemistry from Queen’s University and a Master of Business Administration from the Schulich School of Business. She is an ardent supporter of and advocate for the advancement of women to leadership positions. In recognition of this contribution, she received the Women in Nuclear Canada Leadership Award in 2016.  
Peter Keech, Associate Professor, Department of Chemical Engineering & Applied Chemistry  
Peter Keech is an Associate Professor, Nuclear Engineering within the Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry. For 15 years, he worked at the Nuclear Waste Management Organization where he led research programs around the world to advance the understanding of the container and sealing system that will be used in the deep geological repository for used nuclear fuel in Canada.    
Through work with universities, national laboratories and international partner organizations, he has over one hundred and twenty publications, including more than ninety peer-reviewed journal articles and three book chapters related to chemistry, nuclear waste, corrosion, microbiology and clay.    
Dr. Keech regularly presents both technical and non-technical information directly to scientists, non-scientists, partners and other stakeholders in the nuclear waste program. He provides support and technical review for several organizations, including Nagra of Switzerland, Posiva Oy of Finland, SKB of Sweden and NWS of the United Kingdom and herecently served as a member of the Technical Advisory Committee for NUMO of Japan.    
While at the NWMO and on behalf of its partner academic research community, Dr. Keech co-chaired the committee on Indigenous Knowledge and Western Science within NWMO’s Strategic Initiatives group. He has organized and co-chaired workshops for a wide range of participants, including professors and graduate students, and Indigenous Youth and Elders, to broaden perspectives and meaningfully contribute to Reconciliation. Dr. Keech was born in Orillia, Canada.   
Christina Dimitrov, Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives at OPG  
Christina is a seasoned leader with over two decades of experience at Ontario Power Generation (OPG), where she has held diverse roles across business development, enterprise strategy, treasury and risk management. Currently Christina is a Senior Manager supporting New Growth at OPG, pursuing strategic partnerships in support of the company’s growth portfolio. Christina’s career highlights include contributing to OPG’s corporate strategy development, driving business optimization initiatives, and financing large-scale hydroelectric projects.   
Christina has achieved certifications in risk management, treasury, and project management, complemented by an Honours Bachelor of Commerce. She is a supportive mentor, and advocate for the advancement of women in nuclear and across the energy transition more broadly.  
Moderated by:  Maggie von Vaight, Lecturer, Institute for Studies in Transdisciplinary Engineering Education & Practice   
Maggie von Vaight is a nuclear professional supporting the $13-billion Major Component Replacement (MCR) Program at Bruce Power, one of Canada’s largest clean energy infrastructure investments. The program involves the refurbishment of six nuclear units and is helping secure Ontario’s supply of reliable, carbon-free electricity.  
With more than a decade of experience in the nuclear industry, Maggie has established expertise in procedural governance, project controls, and organizational learning, driving performance and continuous improvement across complex, highly regulated environments. She has served as a lecturer with the University of Toronto, Faculty of Engineering and as a guest lecturer at the University of Guelph, Lang School of Business where her teaching and industry engagement have focused on innovation, commercialization, and entrepreneurship, connecting emerging ideas with industry application.  
An alumna of both the University of Toronto and the University of Guelph, Maggie is a passionate advocate for education, workforce development, and collaboration between academia and industry. Through her leadership and mentorship, she champions opportunities for young professionals, fostering meaningful industry partnerships, and developing the next generation of leaders who will build a stronger, more innovative, and sustainable future.   
Register in advance

title: The Career Confidence & Wellness Series : Overcoming Imposter Syndrome
description:
Have you ever looked at a job posting and thought, “I could never do that”? Or questioned whether you’re actually qualified, even when your experience says otherwise? We’ll explore imposter syndrome and the self-doubt that can show up when applying for jobs, starting a new role, pursuing opportunities, or stepping outside your comfort zone. You’ll learn how to recognize common patterns of imposter syndrome, and identify skills, strengths, and accomplishments you may be overlooking. We’ll also explore how self-compassion can help you increase confidence and trust in yourself.
This program is part of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence and is generously supported by our lead donor Azrieli Foundation along with supporting donors Fidelity Canada, Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter and

title: The Ishizue Award Dinner 2026
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
The JCCC Board of Directors is pleased to announce that the 8th Ishizue Award and accompanying dinner will be held on Thursday November 19, 2026. The Ishizue Award acknowledges and expresses our appreciation and respect to members or friends who have made exceptional contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. The name Ishizue, meaning cornerstone or foundation, pays tribute to the 75 families who, at significant personal financial risk, guaranteed the original mortgage on the JCCC at 123 Wynford Drive in the early 1960’s. These families provided the foundation upon which the JCCC was built, and their support for the JCCC will forever be recognized as the cornerstone for who we are as a community. The recipients of this annual award are a very distinguished group of people who have each made significant life contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. They are: Ken Fukushima: Long time Judo program sensei since 1995 now retired Harry Kawabe: Entertainer from 1970’s at JCCC Caravan and head of clubs such as ukulele and now promotes programming for the Japanese Seniors Akiko Maruoka: Japanese language head instructor since the 60’s Dave Ohashi (posthumous): Photographer and technical support at events for over 40 years Connie Sugiyama: Past JCCC Board member and current Advisor. Founder of Building Together Campaign, Crane Tribute and the Sedai Project David Tsubouchi : Past JCCC Board member from the 80’s, chaired the Antique Road show, a Cabinet Minister and helped strengthen the JCCC and also Sakura Gala Chair over many years. We cordially invite you to honour these distinguished award recipients at an intimate and elegant dinner on Thursday November 19th at 6:30pm at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. Black tie optional. Tickets are $180 each (plus HST) . Maximum of 10 guests per table. To purchase tickets please order through the button below or in person at the JCCC, starting September 21, 2026, and ending November 9, 2026. Please contact Sharon Marubashi for any further information by email or phone (647-291-4751). On behalf of all of the directors of the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, we look forward to spending a special evening of recognition and celebration together. Agenda Cocktails Dinner Evening's Greetings Catering by Spectrum Catering Entertainment Koto Performance by Aiko Fujii Greetings from JCCC President Chris Hope Award Ceremony Group Photo Closing Remarks Aiko Fujii Aiko Fujii started learning at the Ikuta School of Koto and Jiuta Shamisen at an early age. She is a licensed teacher at Kyoto Todokai School of Koto and Shamisen. In addition to performing, she is actively involved in cross-genre collaborations and teaching.

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Oakville Historical Society - Speaker Night "Who Were the Farmerettes?"
location: online
description:
The Oakville Historical Society is pleased to announce the speaker for our last Speaker Night of 2026, a ZOOM virtual presentation, on Thursday, November 19th, presented by Ms. Bonnie Sitter. During 1941 – 1952, approximately 40 thousand girls between the ages of 16 – 18 went to work on Canadian farms during World War II, to maintain critical food production, the program being sponsored by the Canadian Government. 
Please join us to learn the story of how the Famerettes were recruited, where they lived, and how they got to camp. See where the camps were established and what their accommodations were like. After tough days in the fields and orchard, learn how they had fun. Hear the stories of these young women, now in their 90s, explain how they still recall what they often describe as the best summer(s) of their lives. 
Ms. Sitter is a writer with a passion for historical research. She has written for magazines, often exploring agricultural themes. Her co-authored book “Onion Skins and Peach Fuzz – Memories of Ontario Farmerettes” chronicles the experiences of these young women who replaced male farm labour during and after the war. Her book was also developed into a theatrical production by Canadian playwright Ms. Alison Lawrence. 
Ms. Sitter also served as the historical producer for the award winning documentary “We Lend a Hand: The Forgotten Story of Ontario Farmerettes”, which premiered in 2025. This documentary being nominated for the Governor General’s History Award for Excellence in Community Programming. Additionally, she is the proud recipient of the King Charles III Coronation Medal, recognizing her contributions to community and Canadian history. She has been instrumental in having a Provincial Heritage Plaque recognizing the Farmerettes being placed in the Charles Daley Park in Lincoln, Ontario – where the first Farmarette camps were established. 
This event is being presented via Zoom: please join using your own device. 
Members will automatically receive an email containing the link to join the presentation. 
Non members may request a link by sending an email to: oakvillehistory@gmail.com

Qawwali Flamenco marks the long-awaited return of the celebrated collaboration between Pakistani qawwali master Faiz Ali Faiz and flamenco guitar virtuoso Juan Gómez “Chicuelo.”

Following their acclaimed first collaboration a decade ago, Faiz and Gómez reunite to deepen a remarkable artistic dialogue. The first chapter of their Qawwali Flamenco journey explored the relationship between human beings and their beloved; this new creation turns toward the connection between humanity and the divine.

Adaptive Ceramic Histories

The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation Hall. Ground Floor

  Get Tickets



  Become a Member






    
         
    




	



    
        
             
                
                    Curated by Alexandra Box, Gardiner Museum Curatorial Resident 
Engage in an exploration of materially mediated dynamics of care and adaption. Adaptive Ceramic Histories presents an expansive way of looking at histories of medical and adaptive ceramics created for sick or disabled users. The exhibition invites you to delve into the design of care from the vantage point of users, departing from traditional histories of medicine centering on medical professionals. Instead, it considers the possibilities of pleasure and metaphor to build a more fulsome knowledge of patient care to craft the future. 
Adaptive Ceramic Histories features objects from the Gardiner Museum’s permanent collection alongside loans to highlight the importance of ceramic materials at different moments in the history of Western medicine from the 17th century to the present day. 
The Gardiner Museum Curatorial Residency is made possible through the generous support of the Rebanks Family. 

                
                    
    





    
         
    




    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    About the Curator
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box is an arts professional and artist. She has been awarded fellowships and artist residencies through Medalta Potteries, Salt Spring Arts Council, and Point Gallery. Alexandra is a curatorial participant in the Knowledge Incubator & Mentorship Initiative through Redefine Arts. Her writing has been published by Hearth, Peripheral Review, and The Capilano Review. Alexandra serves on the Board at Forest City Gallery and is a contributor to the Media Collaboratory. She holds a BFA (2020) in ceramics and curatorial practices from Emily Carr University and an MA (2024) in Art History from the University of Toronto.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Ageing In Place: How To Assess Your Long Term Care Options
location: North York Central Library, Room 1
description:
Where do you want to spend your retirement years and how can you make that happen?
Looking ahead and having a plan gives us control. Rather than leaving things up to chance, we get to make the choices and decisions that we want--not that someone else wants. Karen Henderson, an expert in long term care options, shares her knowledge and resources to help you make more informed decisions.
As the result of a life changing 14-year dementia care experience, Karen founded the Long Term Care Planning Network, Canada’s leading resource centre for ageing, eldercare and long term care planning and education. Her seminar series, web site and print/electronic tools are recognized as key long term care educational resources for Canadian families.
Karen is a Certified Professional Consultant on Aging (CPCA).

title: Adaptive Ceramic Histories: Opening Reception and Curator Talk
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Adaptive Ceramic Histories: Opening Reception and Curator Talk            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Free Registration                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Friday November 20, 2026
Free with registration 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    5:30 pm: Doors Open
6:00 pm: Curator Talk & Dialogue
7:00 pm: Reception 
Join us to celebrate the opening of the exhibition Adaptive Ceramic Histories with a free curator talk and dialogue with Gardiner Museum Curatorial Resident Alexandra Box, followed by a reception. Box will discuss her research on histories of medical and adaptive ceramics, and how ceramics can guide our thinking and rethinking of sick and disabled people’s material conditions. Following her talk, Box will be in conversation with Senior Curator, Dr. Karine Tsoumis, and Sofia Flores-Ledesma, Programs & Education Coordinator. 
The Gardiner Museum Curatorial Residency is made possible through the generous support of the Rebanks Family. 

                
                    
    

	




			

        
          
          
                        
               
                General : Free
                                        
                        
                                        
                      

                    
          
            
  
            
                                Register Now
              
                        
           
                
                
                    
                        
                    
                
                
          
          
        

	







    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    About the Exhibition 
Adaptive Ceramic Histories presents an expansive way of looking at histories of medical and adaptive ceramics created for sick or disabled users. The exhibition invites you to delve into the design of care from the vantage point of users, departing from traditional histories of medicine centering on medical professionals. Instead, it considers the possibilities of pleasure and metaphor to build a more fulsome knowledge of patient care to craft the future.
Learn more 
  

                
                    
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    About the Curator
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box is an arts professional and artist. She has been awarded fellowships and artist residencies through Medalta Potteries, Salt Spring Arts Council, and Point Gallery. Box is a curatorial participant in the Knowledge Incubator & Mentorship Initiative through Redefine Arts. Her writing has been published by Hearth, Peripheral Review, and The Capilano Review. Box serves on the Board at Forest City Gallery and is a contributor to the Media Collaboratory. She holds a BFA (2020) in ceramics and curatorial practices from Emily Carr University and an MA (2024) in Art History from the University of Toronto.

title: Book launch: Gemma Correll's ANXIETYLAND
location: Lillian H. Smith
description:
Join us for the launch of
ANXIETYLAND
by award-winning popular cartoonist, writer, and illustrator,
Gemma Correll,
chronicling her lifelong experience with anxiety and depression.
With her ingenious and charming illustrations “bursting with personality...peppered with witty asides” (
Publishers Weekly
), Correll leads readers through the amusement park in her own mind—featuring severe anxiety, depression, agoraphobia, and dissociation—a frightening and darkly funny world that “feels like a place apart from ‘real’ life.”
A hilarious thrill ride exploring the mysteries of the mind-body connection, Gemma Correll’s graphic memoir is shot through with the absurd knowledge that there is no linear way through Anxietyland, nor any cure-alls—but there are ways to feel better if you keep trying to move forward.
Gemma will be joined by Peter Birkemoe of The Beguiling Book Store to chat about her book.
Copies of the book will be available for purchase by The Beguiling Book Store.

Friday November 16: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles
Set in Moscow in 1922,
A Gentleman in Moscow
by Amor Towles follows Count Alexander Rostov, a refined Russian aristocrat sentenced by a Bolshevik tribunal to house arrest in the grand Metropol Hotel, where he must spend the rest of his life confined within its walls. As the world outside undergoes dramatic political and social change, the Count gradually transforms his restricted circumstances into a life rich with unexpected friendships, meaningful encounters, and quiet adventures. From navigating the hotel's intricate social world to forming a particularly meaningful bond with a young girl named Nina, Rostov discovers new perspectives on love, loyalty, personal growth, and the passage of time. Elegant, witty, and deeply moving, the novel explores the nature of freedom, the importance of human connection, and the possibility of finding purpose and beauty even when life takes an unexpected turn.

title: Candlelight Fridays (Original Music by Steve Flemming) (Nov. 20th)
description:
Soul City Social Club (Toronto, Canada)
Good day everyone,

Join me for the very first **Candlelight Fridays at The Pheasant**, an intimate evening of original music, storytelling and friendly company in a warm, cozy pub setting.

I'll be sharing a selection of songs I've written over the years, ranging from heartfelt folk and country ballads to soulful melodies, rock and playful satire. My songs are filled with characters searching for love, navigating life's ups and downs, questioning the world around them and sometimes simply laughing at its absurdities.

Along the way, I'll share a few personal stories about what inspired the songs and how they came to life.

So come grab a drink, enjoy some dinner, settle in by candlelight and see where the music takes us!

*We'll also be joined by members of my other social group, so there'll be plenty of friendly company to enjoy the evening with!*

**Event Details:**

**Candlelight Fridays**
*(Original Music by Steve Flemming)*

**Curious about the music?** Listen to some of my original songs on YouTube for a little taste of the music I'll be sharing throughout the evening!
[https://www.youtube.com/@SteveFlemmingSongs](https://www.youtube.com/@SteveFlemmingSongs)

Here's what you can look forward to:

* An evening of original folk, country, soft rock, duets and soulful music.
* Personal stories and inspiration behind selected songs.
* A relaxed, candlelit pub atmosphere with dinner and drinks available.
* Friendly conversation and the opportunity to connect with fellow music lovers.

**Where to Find Us?**

We'll be gathering in the **back dining area** at **The Pheasant: A Firkin Pub**, located at 1999 Avenue Road, approximately six blocks north of Lawrence Avenue and south of Highway 401.
If you're unsure where to go, simply ask the bartender or wait staff for **Steve's event**. They'll be happy to direct you.

**Admission:**
This first evening is **free to attend!**
If you enjoy the music and would like to help support future evenings, there'll be a small tip jar available. Contributions are entirely optional and sincerely appreciated, but most importantly, I'm happy to have you there!

**Friendly Reminders:**

* Please arrive anytime after **6:30 p.m.**
* The Pheasant offers a great dinner menu, along with food and drink specials.
* A minimum purchase of one beverage or appetizer per person is requested to help support the venue.

**Parking and Transportation:**
There's street parking along Avenue Road, as well as free parking on nearby residential side streets where permitted.
The venue is approximately a 15–20-minute walk from Yonge and Lawrence subway station. Alternatively, you can take a bus or Uber from the station.

**About Steve Flemming:**
Steve Flemming is a Canadian songwriter and producer whose original folk, country and story songs explore love, longing, everyday life and the deeper questions of being human. His writing brings together vivid characters, emotional honesty and an enduring curiosity about the lives we lead. As lyricist and producer, Steve shapes each song's story, atmosphere and creative direction, aiming to bring as much life as possible into every song.

I hope you'll join me for what promises to be a relaxing and enjoyable Friday evening of music, stories and good company.

Looking forward to seeing you at The Pheasant!

Sincerely,

Steve Flemming
(Songwriter / Producer / Host)
