title: CANCELLED: Orhan Pamuk's The Museum of Innocence: Novel and Museum
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
IMPORTANT UPDATE:
Due to unforeseen circumstances, this event has been cancelled. We apologize for any inconvenience and look forward to welcoming you to another event soon.
Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk speaks about the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Renowned Turkish novelist and Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk joins celebrated museum and cultural planning leader, Gail Lord, for an extraordinary conversation about one of the most singular acts of imagination in contemporary literature and museology: the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Conceived in tandem with his acclaimed novel of the same name, Pamuk's museum houses the fictional world of his characters Kemal and Füsun in a real, physical space — a small house in Istanbul filled with everyday objects, each one tied to a moment in the novel. The result is a haunting blur between fiction and reality, where a love story lives on not only on the page, but in glass display cases, drawers, and rooms visitors can walk through.
How does one curate a museum for people who never existed? What does it mean to give physical form to memory, longing, and melancholy — the very textures of a novel? And what challenges arise when an author becomes a museum-maker, translating narrative into space, object, and atmosphere?
Orhan Pamuk sits down with Gail Lord, co-founder of Lord Cultural Resources and one of the world's leading museum planners, to discuss the twin creation of the novel and the museum, the ethereal act of turning fiction into physical experience, and what he hoped visitors would feel wandering through the rooms of a story. The conversation will also turn to Pamuk's evolving philosophy of museums — the ideas first laid out in his "Modest Manifesto for Museums" — exploring his belief in small, intimate institutions that honor individual and everyday stories over the grand, monumental narratives so often privileged by national museums.
The discussion will also look ahead to Pamuk's second museum project, currently in development, in which he continues to explore the relationship between storytelling, memory, and collected objects. Building on the foundations laid by the Museum of Innocence, this new endeavor promises to further test the boundaries between literature and lived space, offering fresh insight into how narrative can be translated into an immersive, tangible experience.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

description: DREAMHOUSE is a costume design and voguing dance program for ballroom youth, culminating in a live performance to commemorate Trans Day of Remembrance (TDOR). "DREAMHOUSE" is a play on the Barbie Doll Dreamhouse, referencing both the house structure of ballroom and the ballroom vernacular term "doll." The "doll" of PROTECT THE DOLLS comes from ballroom, not "gay slang" or "Gen Z internet speak," but from the Black trans women who are the heart of ballroom. DREAMHOUSE is a powerful tool of trans activism and artistry, using creative mentorship to spotlight ballroom talent as the epicentre of queer arts and culture. DREAMHOUSE is led by Toronto ballroom community leaders Charlotte Carbone, Diséiye Thompson, Solange Alexander, and Ern In Motion, who are also multi-disciplinary artists in their respective practices of costume design and dance performance. title: Koerner Hall:  Naghash Ensemble, Karen Ouzounian, and the Amadeus Choir
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
**A magical evening of Armenian music direct from Yerevan, and the Canadian premiere of *Dear Mountains*,** a recent work for chorus, solo cello, oud, and percussion, co-composed by the RCM alumna and Silk Road Ensemble member Karen Ouzounian and Lembit Beecher.

Please **use our 15% off promo code** for this concert. Details/Ticket link is below. (Excellent pricing and seats on this concert)

**The Naghash Ensemble** combines the earthy spirituality of Armenian folk songs, new classical music, and contemporary post-minimalism with the energy of rock and jazz. Three brilliant female vocalists and some of Armenia’s finest instrumentalists on duduk, oud, dhol, and piano play captivating new music based on sacred texts by the medieval Armenian mystic poet and priest Mkrtich Naghash.

Written by Armenian-American composer John Hodian, The Naghash Ensemble’s *Songs of Exile* is a profound meditation on man's relationship to God from the perspective of a monk forced to live in exile for many years. Part folk music, part classical, and profoundly moving.

Sought after for her “radiant” (*The New York Times*) performances full of “tremendous heart, bringing joy and a captivating sound to the stage” (*The Strad*), Karen Ouzounian is a Grammy Award nominated cellist and composer who creates music from a deeply personal place. An omnivorous musical spirit who “powerfully shatters pigeonholes with her artistic partners” (*Ravinia Magazine*), she has premiered numerous works and collaborated with some of the most singular musicians of our time, including Yo-Yo Ma, Rhiannon Giddens, and Augustin Hadelich. She will present *Dear Mountains*, a major work composed by her and Lembit Beecher in 2024 that juxtaposes stories told and retold in Ouzounian’s family with scenes of music-making across the Armenian diaspora over the last 100 years, as seen through archival recordings and writings. *Dear Mountains* features Ouzounian on cello, Ara Dinkjian on oud, Philip Mayer on percussion, **and the Amadeus Choir led by Kathleen Allan.**
Led by Artistic Director Kathleen Allan, the Amadeus Choir champions the best of choral music and premieres works of Canadian and international composers through a self-produced Toronto concert series, guest performances, and special events. title: Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab makes its world premiere as a bold new multidisciplinary performance celebrating the enduring connections between cultures through oral and artistic traditions. Led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri, the Amir Amiri Ensemble, featuring Óscar de los Reyes and Esperanza Soria, the performance brings together Canadian and Spanish Andalusian artists in a powerful artistic dialogue. Connected through centuries of migration, poetry, rhythm, and memory, the performance explores a shared cultural legacy while embracing new creative expression. The essentials of flamenco are all present: voice, complex rhythm, and dance.

This presentation ultimately asks how music travels through history, how cultures reshape one another, and how artists continue to carry ancient knowledge into contemporary life. The project seeks to illuminate the enduring connections between Persian and Andalusian artistic worlds, while creating a contemporary performance grounded in research, artistic integrity, and shared humanity.

title: After Dark Fridays (Original Music by Steve Flemming) (Nov. 20th)
description:
Soul City Social Club (Toronto, Canada)
Good day everyone,

Join me for the very first **After Dark Fridays at The Pheasant**, a lively Friday night of upbeat original music, entertaining stories and great company in a warm, welcoming pub setting.

I'll be sharing a selection of songs I've written over the years, with an emphasis on my more upbeat, rhythmic and energetic music. From catchy country-rock and soulful grooves to playful satire, lively duets and songs filled with humour, there's plenty of variety to keep the evening interesting and entertaining.

My songs are filled with colourful characters, unexpected twists, reflections on love and relationships, and observations about the sometimes wonderful, sometimes absurd world we live in.

Along the way, I'll share a few personal stories about what inspired the songs and how they came to life.

So grab a drink, enjoy some dinner, meet some friendly people and settle in for a fun Friday night of original music, laughter and good company!

*We'll also be joined by members of my other social group, so there'll be plenty of friendly company to enjoy the evening with!*

**Event Details:**

**After Dark Fridays**
*(Original Music by Steve Flemming)*

**Curious about the music?** Listen to some of my original songs on YouTube for a little taste of the music I'll be sharing throughout the evening!

[https://www.youtube.com/@SteveFlemmingSongs](https://www.youtube.com/@SteveFlemmingSongs)

Here's what you can look forward to:

* An evening of upbeat original country-rock, soulful music, lively duets and playful satire.
* Personal stories, humour and inspiration behind selected songs.
* A fun, relaxed pub atmosphere with dinner and drinks available.
* Friendly conversation, mingling and the opportunity to connect with fellow music lovers.

**Where to Find Us?**

We'll be gathering in the **back dining area** at **The Pheasant: A Firkin Pub**, located at 1999 Avenue Road, approximately six blocks north of Lawrence Avenue and south of Highway 401.

If you're unsure where to go, simply ask the bartender or wait staff for **Steve's event**. They'll be happy to direct you.

**Admission:**

This first evening is **free to attend!**

If you enjoy the music and would like to help support future evenings, there'll be a small tip jar available. Contributions are entirely optional and sincerely appreciated, but most importantly, I'm happy to have you there!

**Friendly Reminders:**

* Please arrive anytime after **9:00 p.m.**
* The Pheasant offers a great dinner menu, along with food and drink specials.
* A minimum purchase of one beverage or appetizer per person is requested to help support the venue.

**Parking and Transportation:**

There's street parking along Avenue Road, as well as free parking on nearby residential side streets where permitted.

The venue is approximately a 15–20-minute walk from Yonge and Lawrence subway station. Alternatively, you can take a bus or Uber from the station.

**About Steve Flemming:**

Steve Flemming is a Canadian songwriter and producer whose original folk, country and story songs explore love, longing, everyday life and the deeper questions of being human. His writing brings together vivid characters, emotional honesty and an enduring curiosity about the lives we lead. As lyricist and producer, Steve shapes each song's story, atmosphere and creative direction, aiming to bring as much life as possible into every song.

I hope you'll join me for what promises to be a fun and enjoyable Friday night of upbeat music, entertaining stories and great company.

Looking forward to seeing you at The Pheasant!

Sincerely,

Steve Flemming
(Songwriter / Producer / Host)

title: 🍁Fall Hike: Long Branch GO to Port Credit GO🍁
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
# 🍁 Fall Hike: Long Branch GO to Port Credit GO

Join us for a scenic lakeside hike along the beautiful Waterfront Trail, from Long Branch GO Station to Port Credit GO Station!

We’ll explore a mix of parks, beaches, and tree-lined paths, taking in the crisp autumn air, colourful leaves, and classic Lake Ontario views. This is the first time our group has done this particular route, so come along and help us welcome the fall season!

We’ll take our time, with stops for photos, snacks, and conversation along the way. This is a social hike rather than a race, but please be prepared to walk for a few hours. We’ll finish in Port Credit, where we’ll take the GO train back toward Toronto.

***

### 🚆 Meetup Details — Choose Your Starting Point

**Option 1: Meet in Toronto and travel together**
📍 **Meeting location:** Outside the main doors of the Fairmont Royal York on Front Street West.

* **10:15 AM:** Meet outside the hotel. Look for my Moose Hat! 🦌
* **10:30 AM sharp:** We’ll leave for the station.
* **10:45 AM:** Planned train departure.

Please arrive on time. We cannot hold the train for latecomers, and once we’ve left, you’ll need to make your own way to the starting point if you miss us.

**Option 2: Meet us at Long Branch GO Station**

📍 **Meeting location:** Long Branch GO Station, **by the station exit closest to the parking lot**.

This is our starting point for the hike. Please meet me by that exit and look for the Moose Hat! 🦌

* **Around 11:00 AM:** Arrive and find the group.
* **11:15 AM:** We’ll begin the walk.

Please use the specified exit rather than waiting elsewhere around the station. We had some confusion with the meeting point previously, so make sure you know where to find us.

**Important:** This is a point-to-point hike. We’ll finish at **Port Credit GO Station**, not Long Branch. We will not walk back to Long Branch.

### 🥾 The Walk

We’ll follow the Waterfront Trail through a mix of waterfront scenery, parks, beaches, and paths. We’ll take occasional breaks for photos, snacks, and conversation, with time to enjoy the views and each other’s company.

Please wear comfortable walking shoes and be prepared for a few hours on your feet. Bring your own water and snacks; you’re welcome to bring something extra to share.

### 🚆 Getting Back

We expect to start wrapping up around **2:00 PM**, with our destination being Port Credit GO Station.

We’ll take the GO train from Port Credit toward Toronto. **Please check the GO schedule for the event date before attending.** Not every train necessarily stops at Long Branch, so do not assume you can take the train back there to retrieve a car. If you’re driving and parking at Long Branch, check your return options in advance.

### 💲 Meetup Fee

The Meetup fee is **$5**, payable in cash in person or by e-transfer to **[mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)**.
GO train fares are additional. Check the current fare for your journey.

### 🎒 What to Bring

* Water
* Comfortable walking shoes
* Snacks or something small for our breaks
* A camera or phone for the fall colours
* Weather-appropriate clothing

### ⚠️ Please Note

* This event is weather-dependent only if conditions make the walk unsafe. Keep an eye on the event page for any updates or cancellation notices.
* You’re welcome to leave early, but please let me know so I know you’ve left the group.
* If you’re joining at Long Branch, make sure you use the **station exit closest to the parking lot**.
* This is a one-way walk ending at Port Credit. Please plan your transportation accordingly.

### 👥 About the Group

Whether you’re single or partnered, you’re welcome to join us to get outdoors, meet people, and make connections. We also organize movies, walks, hikes, arts and culture outings, restaurant visits, and plenty more.
Organized by Mathew. Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**.

🍁 Enjoy the trail. Take in the views. Meet some new people.

title: Kashikari-Inspired Tile Glazing Workshop | Misbah Ahmed & Tigerbaby Coffee & Clay
location: Tigerbaby Coffee & Clay, 977 College St, Toronto, ON M6H 1A6, Canada
description:
Join sukoon space, ceramic artist Misbah Ahmed https://misbahahmed.com/?utm_source=luma and Tigerbaby Coffee and Clay https://tigerbabycc.com/?utm_source=luma for an afternoon of tile glazing inspired by Kashikari.

Taking the colours and patterns of Kashikari tilework as a starting point, you’ll explore your own design on a handmade ceramic tile. Misbah will guide you through the glazing process, working on an approximately 7 × 7-inch tile that has been prepared and fired ahead of the workshop.

Spend an afternoon making, experimenting with pattern and connecting with others, while creating a piece of your own. All glazing materials, guided instruction and final kiln firing are included.

About Kashikari

Kashikari is the art of glazed ceramic tilework, with roots in Persian ceramic traditions and a distinctive heritage in Multan, Pakistan. Multani tilework is known for its cobalt blues, turquoise and white, combining intricate floral motifs and geometric patterns to decorate shrines and historic buildings.

In this workshop, we’ll take inspiration from that tradition as you glaze your own handmade, pre-fired ceramic tile. Misbah will guide you through exploring colour and pattern, with room to interpret the designs in your own way.

Artist Bio

Misbah Ahmed is a Toronto-based artist and educator working across ceramics, painting and printmaking. Born in Islamabad and raised in Canada, she draws on Pakistani and South Asian stories, family histories and archival research to explore belonging, cultural change and our relationship with the environment.

Her work brings an interest in traditional crafts into conversation with themes of memory, resilience and the climate crisis. She graduated from OCAD University’s Illustration program in 2018, receiving its program medal, and has taught there since 2020. She also teaches ceramics at the Gardiner Museum and founded Sehn Studio in 2024, a Toronto space for art-making, classes and guest workshops. Her solo exhibitions include Dry Thunder at the Art Gallery of Burlington in 2025.

title: Disaster Day
description:
Are you, or someone you know, interested in floods, wildfires, climate change, emergency response, technology such as VR and drones, public safety, or helping communities prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters?
Join us for Disaster Day 2026 a free interactive event designed specifically for high school students, young adults, and those curious about the exciting world of disaster and emergency management as well as research on crises and disasters. Learn about disaster-related studies at York University, including connections to many disciplines such as health, engineering, law, public administration, sociology, etc.
📅 Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026
🕐 Time: 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
📍 Location: York University, Keele Campus (exact location will be shared upon registration)
Through hands-on activities, demonstrations, and conversations with professionals and researchers, participants will discover how communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.

🔥 Wildfire Community Challenge Work together as part of an emergency management team to protect a community during a simulated wildfire scenario. Explore the decisions emergency managers must make under pressure and see how collaboration can save lives and reduce impacts.
🚁 Virtual Reality and Drone Demonstrations See how cutting-edge technologies are used to assess damage, monitor hazards, support emergency response, and help communities reduce disaster risk.
🌪️ How Scientists Predict and Communicate Risk Learn how mathematicians, emergency managers, and researchers use science to predict and communicate hazard impacts.
📋 What Is It Like to Be an Emergency Manager? Meet professionals working in disaster and emergency management and explore possible career pathways in public safety, emergency planning, risk reduction, and community resilience.
🏢 Community Partner Showcase Connect with organizations working on disaster preparedness, emergency response, and humanitarian assistance, including:
Canadian Red Cross 
Team Rubicon Canada 
Emergency Management Ontario
Additional community and emergency management partners
🔍 Disaster Day Scavenger Hunt Explore the event while completing challenges and learning activities. All participants who complete the scavenger hunt will be entered into a draw for a $100 prize.
Registration is free, but spaces are limited.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: Introduction to Chainmail Workshop
location: Lillian H. Smith, Bagshaw Room, 1st floor.
description:
Chainmail, the ancient art of linking metal rings together in a chain or mesh weave, has a long history within cultural practices from all over the world. These days you might not need a piece of armour to protect yourself during a swordfight, but you still might want to know how to make some - whether for yourself or to deck out a favourite toy! Or, maybe you want to make some unique jewelry: bracelets, necklaces, or earrings. Why not both?
Registration for both sessions is required:
1st session, Nov 7: Basics! Opening and closing rings, Japanese 1-in-1, 2-in-2, or 3-in-3 chain weave, attaching clasps. Make a bracelet or a short necklace.
2nd session, Nov 21: Pick 1 option - barrel or box chain weave, or 4-1 European mesh weave. Make a bracelet, a short necklace, or a base for a larger piece.
Please note that chainmail requires repetitive hand motions, gripping, and close visual attention to detail.
These sessions are oriented towards beginners but more advanced learners are also welcome.

Ryan Kelln

We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it.
Featuring:
Alex Olson

Khasir Hean

title: ROM Discounted - Tour, World Wildlife Photography + Other Exhibits
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Saturday November 21st,** **join me at the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) to take a Museum Tour, visit the World Wildlife Photography Exhibit, the Crawford Lake Exhibit and Cloudscape Installation.** Be among the first in Canada to see this year’s winners and finalists of the annual *[Wildlife Photographer of the Year](https://www.rom.on.ca/whats-on/exhibitions/wildlife-photographer-year-2026)* 2026 competition. Attendees can see any exhibits of interest. **Purchase your ticket for Saturday November 21st. We will be heading out for dinner after at the number 1 Chinese restaurant in Canada. This is a separate event and you can sign up [here](https://www.meetup.com/experiencetoronto/events/316869554/) if you'd like to join us.**

**Museum Highlights Tour**
Explore the wonders of ROM in a 45-minute tour that brings iconic objects to life. Enjoy highlights of arts, culture and nature… throughout the world and throughout time.

**Cloudscape Installation**
*Cloudscape* is a mesmerizing installation that blends traditional artistry with contemporary themes. Immerse yourself in Yan's floating masterpiece, where each sculpted cloud tells a story of cultural heritage and environmental consciousness, and invites us to reflect on our relationship with nature.

**World Wildlife Photography**
Each year, the annual competition - organized by the Natural History Museum in London, UK - receives tens of thousands of image submissions from aspiring wildlife photographers of all ages. One hundred selected images from this year's competition - unforgettable photographs of wildlife and the natural world - will travel to ROM right after the winners are announced. Experience the power of photography to reveal, connect, and transform our view of nature.

description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:

description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:** [\[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fS35YSjopjE)

📖 **📖 Plot Summary:** The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping revisits the world of Panem and follows young Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

***

🎫 Buy your ticket here: [https://www.cineplex.com](https://www.cineplex.com)
📍🪑 **Where I will be sitting:**

Yes, we’re heading out after! It’s not just a movie night — it’s a social night. Let's talk, laugh, and dissect every plot twist.

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Flamenco: Made in Canada presents Duende Al Nur
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Duende al Nur , meaning “Duende toward the light,” is an immersive flamenco work where light, shadow and fire transform the dancing body.

Performed on a luminous plexiglass platform, the piece explores light as a sacred, living force rising from beneath the dancer. From darkness, the body is awakened by illumination. Breath becomes pulse, pulse becomes rhythm, and rhythm becomes flamenco. Through footwork, castanets, zills, breath and silence, Carmen Romero moves through a ritual journey of awakening and renewal. Rooted in the emotional power of duende and the Arabic resonance of nur, the work becomes a passage through memory, prayer, rhythm and transformation.

The work draws from flamenco’s emotional intensity, rhythmic complexity and theatrical power while opening the performance space to Arabic resonance, sacred illumination and immersive sound. Rather than presenting cultural influence literally, Duende al Nur approaches these elements as echoes, atmospheres and poetic points of connection.

title: Sonic Sancocho - Edición Simulacro Decembrino
location: DROM Taberna, 458 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5V 2A8, Canada
description:
Join us at Drom Taberna with performances by Champetapunk and David Labrada Ensemble!

We're back at our beloved Drom Taberna for a night celebrating autumn, diverse sounds from across Latin America and our signature Sancocho - three things to keep your soul warm as the seasons change.

Sonic Sancocho is thrilled to welcome special guest selector from Colombia, Solano Patiño https://www.instagram.com/solanopatino/ , who will deliver vibrant DJ sets to be broadcast live on his celebrated radio show, Champetapunk https://www.instagram.com/champetapunk/ , and live performances by Toronto-based, acclaimed David Labrada Ensemble https://www.instagram.com/david.labrada.1/ , bringing the spirit of Havana and flavours of the diasporas to the stage, in sound.

As always, Founders, Juana Go-gó https://instagram.com/gogojuana and olasconola https://instagram.com/olasconola will share a bold blend of music to welcome you to the party.

Complimentary cup of Sancocho at midnight for ticket holders - please note: first come, first served.

What is Sancocho? Learn more about the history here https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sancocho .

Advance Eventbrite ticket holders must check in to the venue by 10:30 pm.

Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026
Doors: 10:30 pm
Music: 11:00 pm - 4:00 am
Location: DROM Taberna - 458 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON, Canada

About Sonic Sancocho:
The spice of life in sound, shared with community. Much like ingredients in a universal dish - a big pot of soup - here, platters of sound are spun and served with warm welcome. Musical ingredients from around the world, from a local perspective, for all to share and enjoy. Founded by selectresses olasconola http://instagram.com/olasconola & http://instagram.com/gogojuana Juana Go-gó https://instagram.com/gogojuana in Toronto, Canada, Sonic Sancocho is a community gathering of music and food - two things that nourish heart and soul. They bring forth the B Sides and the beloved of Latin music, with sounds from around the world, to your venue through all-vinyl DJ sets and dynamic live performances. Sancocho is where all of the ingredients come together and are shared amongst one another - from the starches to the spices and everything in between. We turn up the heat to bring it to a boil, coming together to enjoy a moment of connection through a serving of soup, within layers of sound, endless movement and fun.

Tune in to the radio show https://ciut.fm/sonicsancocho/ , hosted & produced by Juana Go-gó https://instagram.com/gogojuana - Sundays at 2:00 pm ET on CIUT 89.5 FM!

About Solano Patiño | Champetapunk:

Solano Patiño is a selector, record collector and researcher of Afro-Caribbean and world music. He is the founder and director of Radio Estruendo Tinansucá, Bogotá’s free, experimental, community-driven and portable radio, and creator of Champetapunk, a party and research project on African diaspora culture and rebel sounds, running since 2013 between Bogotá and Mexico City. His radio work has taken him across Asia, Africa, North Africa and the Caribbean, where he has relentlessly dug through markets and record shops in search of vinyl. This set is built mainly from those finds on 7″: Afro-Caribbean and world music.

About David Labrada:
David Labrada More is a Toronto-based performer, composer, music educator, and music producer. He will be joining a roster of acclaimed pedagogues and guest artists in August 2025 at The Royal Conservatory of Music’s inaugural Summer Piano Performance Intensive for high school students, where he will be teaching improvisation.

David is an award-winning musician and composer, winning First Place in the National Youth Jazz Competition in Havana, Cuba three years consecutively (2006-2008). As an educator with experience in both classroom and private instruction, David teaches jazz piano, voice, percussion, music theory, songwriting, and music production. He has developed curriculum for private school music programs, including ensemble direction for band and choir. He also has experience teaching music from Junior Kindergarten to Grade 8 as outlined by The Ontario Curriculum.

Founder of DLM.Music Production, David works with local and international artists including Ernesto del Alma (Canada), Irene Miguel (UK), Adonis Puentes (BC), Cassava Latin Band (Canada), Joel Sierra (Mexico), Mario y su timbeco (US), and Edglish (Azerbaijani).

David has a Bachelor of Music in Composition from Higher Institute of Art (Havana, Cuba) and a Bachelor of Arts in Music from the University of Toronto.

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesday)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
### 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂

Join us for a beautiful fall walk through Hogg’s Hollow, one of Toronto’s charming historic neighbourhoods tucked away in North York. With its winding roads, forested trails, stone bridges, and scenic ravines, this area feels like a hidden village in the middle of the city — especially when the leaves turn golden and the air starts to feel like autumn.

We’ll explore the valley around the Don River West Branch, taking in the neighbourhood’s natural beauty and historic character. Along the way, we’ll touch on the story of James Hogg, the Scottish settler associated with the area’s early mill, and the tragic **Hogg’s Hollow Disaster of 1960**, when five workers lost their lives during tunnel construction.

After our walk, we’ll head to **Swiss Chalet** for lunch, because nothing says fall like comfort food and good company! 🍗

### 📍 Meetup Location — Please Read Carefully!

**We’re meeting directly in front of the Shell gas station store entrance.**
Please stand **right in front of the entrance to the store**, where people walk in and out.
Look for my famous Moose Hat! 🦌

### 🕒 Meetup Details

* **Meeting time:** 11:00 AM
* **Departure:** 11:05 AM sharp. I’ll wait a maximum of five minutes.
* **Ending location:** We’ll return to our starting point, making it convenient for anyone arriving by transit or car.
* **Meetup fee:** $5, payable in cash or by e-transfer to **[mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)**.

### 🥾 What to Bring

* Water
* Comfortable walking shoes
* A snack if you’d like something before lunch
* Weather-appropriate clothing

☔ **Rain or shine!** There’s no such thing as bad weather — just inappropriate clothing.

### 👥 About the Group

Whether you’re single or partnered, you’re welcome to join us to get outdoors, meet people, and make connections. We also organize movies, walks, hikes, arts and culture outings, restaurant visits, and plenty more.
**You can RSVP ahead of time or show up on the day** if you’re not sure you can make it.

Organized by Mathew. Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**.

🍂 Enjoy the walk. Stay for lunch. Leave with new connections.

location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

description:

The only authorized cemeteries within York were Anglican or Roman Catholic. Citizens who did not belong to either church had no choice but to find burial arrangements outside York.

The General Burying Ground received Royal Assent in 1826 and land that came to be known as Potters Field was acquired and started operation soon afterwards. Over time, additional cemetery lands were added and in 1873, a new cemetery available to all citizens was established. The new cemetery was situated on the farm land of the Cawthra family near Yonge Street.

This walk is for all fitness levels. Please dress for the weather. This walk will begin and end outside the Yorkminster Park Baptist Church at 1585 Yonge Street just north of Heath Street.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person! This tour has space for **11** explorers, so if you do plan on attending please secure your tickets early.

title: Look to Windward - Ian M. Banks
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

So glad to have our Iain M. Banks selection finalized for November. As we’ve discussed previously, the books in the Culture series are connected, but don’t necessarily need to be read in order. The Club really enjoyed Book 2, *The Player of Games*, and I’m curious to see where in the universe we land with Book 7, 2000’s *Look to Windward*.

[sophyanempire](https://sophyanempire.wordpress.com/2012/03/08/look-to-windward-iain-m-banks-orbit-2000/) has a solid review of this entry in the Culture series, calling *Look to Windward* “exciting, tense, sad and heroic.” She notes that from there, “the book grows in scope, showing multiple perspectives, almost all of them from a non-human alien point of view.”

[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2000/sep/02/sciencefictionfantasyandhorror.iainbanks) also has a great review from when the book was first published. Phil Daoust writes that “Banks has tremendous fun with his giant canvas” in *Windward*.

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

A reminder that Book Club takes a break each October, so while Look to Windward has a fairly large page count, we’ll essentially have two months to read our pick.

Cheers,

Jon

description: This listing is for a two session Beginner Crochet Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday November 22nd and 29th from 2:30pm-4:00pm Learn the fundamentals of crochet in this two part class. We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Pursue Peace: Contemporary Chamber Music by Canadian Jewish Composers, An Album Release Concert
location: Accolade East Building, Tribute Communities Recital Hall @ 83 York Boulevard, Toronto
description:
Free admission. Register on our Eventbrite:
https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/pursue-peace-contemporary-chamber-music-by-canadian-jewish-composers-tickets-2001068522819 ( https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/pursue-peace-contemporary-chamber-music-by-canadian-jewish-composers-tickets-2001068522819 )
Album Release Celebration Concert
York University’s Koschitzky Centre for Jewish Studies and the Department of Music in the School of the Arts, Media, Performance and Design invite you to the opening of the fifth season of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York, with a special release concert celebrating Pursue Peace, the initiative’s debut album. The program brings together the work of three distinguished Canadian composers and leading performers in an evening of music shaped by memory, identity, history, and the many ways music gives voice to human experience.
Released by New Focus Recordings, the New York-based independent label devoted to contemporary and creative music, Pursue Peace features composers Noam Lemish (ON), Sid Robinovitch (MB), and James Rolfe (ON), whose music spans intimate works for violin and piano, string quartet and clarinet, and a larger work for choir, soprano and ensemble.
More than three years in the making, the album is the culmination of an ongoing artistic collaboration at York, bringing the work of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York to a wider audience. We invite you to join the ongoing conversation through music and celebrate this milestone with us.
Featuring:
Amy Hillis, violin, Katherine Dowling, piano, Sara Schabas, soprano, David Fallis, conductor, Maya Lahyani, mezzo-soprano, Noam Lemish, piano, Anthony Thompson, clarinet, Ilana Waniuk, violin, Carol Gimbel, viola, Mark Chambers, cello, Clark Schaufele, chamber organ, Nathan Petitpas, percussion, Jane Fingler, soprano, Vania Chan, soprano, Veronika Muggeridge, alto, Rebecca Claborn, alto, Laura Chambers, flute, Cheryl Duval, piano.
Program:
Adieu Babylon by Sid Robinovitch
Di Mezinkeh by Sid Robinovitch
Pursue Peace by Noam Lemish
Selections from Blood and Water by James Rolfe
O Greenest Branch by James Rolfe
“Sound and Sense: Jewish Music @ York” is a performance and lecture series dedicated to showcasing the multicultural diversity of Jewish musical expression as well as the ongoing intersections between Jewish and non-Jewish musical practices and communities. The initiative is driven by an inclusive philosophy that believes in the power of music to serve as a bridge-builder and a vehicle for cultural exchange and dialogue.
Parking is available at the Student Services Parking Garage (15 James Gillies St, North York, ON).
The Accolade East Building is located immediately outside the York University subway station (TTC line 1) in front of the left hand exit.
The series has been made possible via the generous support of the Azrieli Foundation.

title: Los Magníficos
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
“Los Magníficos” is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the greatness of contemporary flamenco. Five outstanding artists come together in a unique performance where singing, dance, guitar, and piano reach their highest expression.

Sandra Carrasco, one of the most important voices of the moment, takes us to the very heart of flamenco. David de Arahal captivates audiences with his mastery of the guitar, while Andrés Barrios transforms the piano into pure emotion. Dancer “El Yiyo” embodies the power and intensity of flamenco, joined by Carmen “La Talegona,” whose artistry and magnetic stage presence bring elegance, strength, and depth to this extraordinary encounter.

Prepare for an intense and magnetic journey, where energy and sensitivity intertwine in an explosion of talent. “ Los Magníficos” is not just a performance; it’s a unique opportunity to witness the union of some of the finest artists of our time in a moment destined to remain forever in the memory of flamenco art.

description: In this class, you’ll learn the basics of using an Apple device. You’ll explore its different parts, understand what an operating system is, and learn how to turn it on. You’ll also get familiar with the home screen, how to adjust settings, and how iCloud and storage work.

title: Benefits and Credits for Adults 65 Years & Older
location: Don Mills, Auditorium
description:
This presentation by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) provides an overview of the income sources, benefits, credits, and tax measures available to seniors. It explains retirement income programs such as Old Age Security (OAS), the Canada Pension Plan (CPP), and private pensions, and highlights the importance of filing a tax return every year to receive benefit payments and maintain eligibility for programs.
The presentation also covers key tax credits and deductions available to seniors, including the Age Amount, Pension Income Amount, Medical Expense Tax Credit, Home Accessibility Tax Credit, Disability Tax Credit, and pension income splitting. In addition, it shares information on free tax-filing assistance.
Drop in.  No registration required.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

title: Growing Native Plants From Seed
location: Cliffcrest
description:
Growing native plants from seed is an inexpensive and easy way to add plants to your garden – but you need to start early! Many native plants require several months of cold temperatures to sprout in the spring. Join this session with Toronto Master Gardeners to learn where to get your seed and how to sow it over the winter for germination in the spring. At the end of the program, native seeds will be given out to attendees, while supplies last. Suitable for gardeners of any skill level, with any kind of outdoor space.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile
Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: The Stories We Keep: A Writing and Storytelling Workshop
location: Wychwood Library, 1431 Bathurst Street, Toronto, ON M5R 3J2, Canada
description:
Bring an object that matters to you and spend an afternoon exploring its story through writing, reflection, and conversation.

The Stories We Keep is a guided writing and storytelling workshop about the memories, people, places, and moments held within the objects we keep.

For this workshop, you’ll be invited to bring one meaningful object from home and use it as a starting point for writing and reflection. Led by a former archaeologist, the workshop draws on archaeology-informed approaches to explore the stories, memories, and meaning we attach to the things we keep. Through a series of prompts, exercises, and conversation, we’ll explore the story behind your object and the memories connected to it.

No previous writing experience is needed. You don’t need to consider yourself a writer. Just bring an object that means something to you and an openness to see where its story takes you. Sharing your object’s story is encouraged, but not mandatory for the experience.

What to Expect

• A relaxed, small-group writing workshop

• Guided prompts and writing exercises inspired by archaeology and personal storytelling

• Workbook, writing materials, object description card, and photograph will be provided.

• Time to reflect, write, and share as much or as little as you feel comfortable with

• Conversation about memory, objects, and the stories we attach to the things we keep

• A chance to leave with new writing about an object that matters to you


What to Bring

One meaningful object to write about. It can be anything: a piece of jewellery, an old photograph, a childhood toy, a handwritten note, a souvenir, a trinket, a tool, a book, or something completely ordinary that holds a special memory.

The object does not need to be valuable or old. What matters is the story it carries for you.


Who Is It For?

The Stories We Keep is for anyone interested in personal storytelling, memory, objects, and creative writing. Whether you already love to write or haven't picked up a pen in years, the workshop is designed to meet you where you are.

Come curious, come nostalgic, come with an object and a story you haven't quite put into words yet.

title: Indie Press Fiction Night
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, for an evening of Indie Press fiction, featuring Stella Harvey, Jon Redfern, and Denise Roig.
About the Books:
Disruption
by Stella Leventoyannis Harvey
Young Kitianna has always been curious about what life is like on the other side of the wall that divides her war-scarred country. When her actions draw the scrutiny of the authorities, Kitianna’s parents realize the only way to keep her from being forced into a re-education camp is to send her away.
But while they may have secured their daughter’s safety, at least for now, the underground protest movement against the government is getting stronger, and the regime’s reaction has been to double down on draconian security measures. It seems no one is safe from the droids and the drones and the surveillance that is everywhere.
Disruption
asks how much freedom we’re willing to relinquish for the sake of security. And when the government is secretly controlled by oligarchs, how can ordinary citizens fight back and reclaim their liberties?
The Ogre Club
by Jon Redfern
Richard Suttle's just taken a detour from his quiet life as a fraud investigator in Winnipeg--into the heart of Mexico City's dark underworld. His mission? Find Brendan Thorst, the reckless 22-year-old son of his ailing high school friend.
Brendan's no saint. He's a spoiled troublemaker who vanished after raising the ire of brutal cartels and street dealers by selling drugs to unsuspecting tourists. But that's only the surface.
The real story is far more twisted--and deadly. Brendan's on the run after threatening to expose a powerful televangelist who's hiding a horrifying secret: a kiddy porn operation protected by corrupt cops and blind faith.
Now Suttle must navigate a lethal maze of deception, violence, and betrayal. Because in this city, the only thing more dangerous than the criminals is the man who's supposed to be on your side.
Gathered Here
by Denise Roig
Is it too late to make peace with one’s choices?
To marry or not to marry.
Three generations of women in southern Ontario ponder what’s in it for them. Karin, a millennial, her fifty-something Aunt Sheena, and Jane, Karin’s grandmother, narrate their separate, but linked, stories of love, weddings, loss, and a little mayhem.
Can love – imperfect, unpredictable, human – really conquer all?

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.

title: Online Info Session & Panel: MEng Co-op in CivMin
location: Online
description:
👉Register here to join event 
Join us for a dynamic presentation and panel discussion with current CivMin MEng Coop students!  You won’t want to miss this opportunity to learn more about the MEng Co-op program from Sebastian Goodfellow (Associate Chair – Professional Programs) and representatives from the Engineering Career Centre, plus gain insight from MEng Co-op students who are currently completing their Co-op placement. 
Panelists will share their experiences + attendees will have a chance to ask questions about the program and connect directly with panelists in an engaging Q&A session. 
Meet our Panelists:
Nabin Basnet
Nabin Basnet holds a Bachelor of Civil Engineering from Tribhuvan University in Nepal. He moved to Ontario in 2024 and joined UofT’s MEng with Co-op program to build on his engineering background and get hands-on experience in the Canadian industry. He is focusing on Waterpower and the ELITE emphasis, which lets him sharpen both his technical skills and his leadership. He is currently working as a Technical Trainee at Toronto Water division of City of Toronto. His proudest moment so far is that he and his daughter (now 5 years young) started school in Canada on the same day, she in Junior Kindergarten and he in his Master’s at UofT and he loves that they’re learning side by side as they settle into this new chapter. She has even sat in on about 15 hours of his lectures at UofT. 
 
Bahar Shahkaram
Bahar Shahkaram completed her Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering at the University of Tehran and is now pursuing a Master of Engineering in Civil Engineering at the University of Toronto, focusing on transportation planning and data analytics.  She chose the MEng for its practical focus, and the co-op option sealed the decision. Her co-op is with York Region, where she works on transportation planning and forecasting. Day to day, that means GIS, traffic data, and building tools that help planners compare scenarios and make sense of the numbers.  Bahar started her degree thinking she would end up designing structures, but ended up hooked on why people travel the way they do. 
Angela Zhou
Angela Zhou is currently pursuing a Master of Engineering (MEng) in Civil Engineering at the University of Toronto, having completed an undergraduate degree in Civil Engineering at the University of British Columbia. Angela is currently completing an eight-month co-op placement with the City of Toronto as a Technical Trainee on the Asset Data team within the Water Infrastructure Management division. Angela chose to pursue an MEng to explore areas of civil engineering beyond those covered during her undergraduate studies, and accepted a co-op opportunity to gain practical, hands-on experience. Growing up, Angela loved spending time at the beaches along Lake Ontario. Now, Angela gets to be part of the work that helps bring that same water into homes across Toronto through the city’s water infrastructure system!

location: Joan Goldfarb Study Centre, 275 Joan & Martin Goldfarb Centre for Fine Arts @ 86 Fine Arts Road, Toronto
description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Everyday Courage, Everyday Resilience: Finding your resilient flow in times of change and complexity
description:
Join us for an interactive discussion with Career Coach in Residence Sangeetha Dikshit and guest speaker, Abirambika Ravivarman. Resilience is more than bouncing back, it's our capacity to navigate change, uncertainty, and challenges with greater awareness, adaptability, and purpose. In this interactive session, participants will explore the concept of Resilient Flow and how our beliefs, habits, and ways of making sense of the world influence how we respond under pressure.
Sangeetha Dikshit
, one of TPL's four Career Coaches in Residence. Sangeetha is a Career and Leadership Coach empowering individuals to navigate career transitions, develop in-demand skills, and achieve professional success.
Abirambika Ravivarman
is a Human-Centric Leadership and Systems Coach and the founder of Human Systems at Work. Her work goes beyond individual behaviour to focus on the deeper relational dynamics that shape team performance and culture. In today’s AI-augmented workplace, she emphasizes the importance of strengthening the Human Edge—the presence-based and relational capabilities that enable leaders and teams to thrive in complexity.

In this workshop, participants will be guided by artist Farooq Zia through step-by-step instructions using drawing tools and watercolour paint to create their own geometric pattern and complex design art pieces.

title: Canoe with Us? Indigenous Education & Research
location: 280N York Lanes
description:
This panel discussion brings together Indigenous scholars to share insights, experiences, and future directions in education and research. It serves as an invitation to all faculty and graduate students to build relationships, share common goals, and explore future collaborations.
 Key Discussion Themes:

Faculty Reflections: Personal insights into their journeys as Indigenous Faculty members.
Research Horizons: Current achievements and future research trajectories
Graduate Support: Pathways for the mentorship and support of graduate students
Collaborative Alliances: Roles, partnerships, and meaningful collaborations with non-Indigenous counterparts

 Facilitator:

Angel Alook: Director of the Centre for Indigenous Knowledges and Languages (CIKL), and Associate Professor in the School of Gender, Sexuality and Women’s Studies

Panelists:

John Hupfield: Wuleelham Director, overseeing the Waaban Indigenous Teacher Education program, examines powwow as a place to enact pedagogy, praxis, and knowledges in grounding community through culture and land
Rebecca Beaulne-Stuebing: Assistant Professor whose research focuses on Indigenous education and community-grounded learning, including a community medicines sovereignty project
Jesse Staats: Assistant Professor, explores Indigenous experiences and approaches to transforming governance relationships between universities and Indigenous Peoples

title: National Housing Day: A Film Screening and Panel Discussion of Seeking Shelter
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (1st floor)
description:
On November 24
th
, join Homeless Connect Toronto at the Toronto Reference Library for a special premiere screening and community conversation celebrating the launch of Seeking Shelter, a documentary series by filmmaker Nadine Valcin.
As Canada continues to grapple with a growing housing crisis, Seeking Shelter shines a light on the people, organizations, and grassroots movements creating innovative and inclusive solutions to housing instability. Through stories of resilience, collaboration, and community action, the series explores what becomes possible when people come together to reimagine housing.
This special event will feature premiere screenings of:
Episode 2: Communal Land for the Common Good :
Toronto’s Parkdale Neighbourhood Land Trust is sowing the seeds for innovative housing and communal growth.
And
Episode 4: Co-ops and the Power of Community:
Since the 1970s, a Toronto co-operative has modelled a collaborative and people-first approach to housing.
Following the screenings, TVO's Nam Kiwanuka will moderate a panel discussion with housing subject-matter experts, exploring the themes raised in the films and the future of community-driven housing solutions. Audience members will also have an opportunity to participate in a Q&A and contribute reflections to a collaborative poll. Panelists are: Nadine Valcin, the award winning filmmaker, Dominique Russell, Executive Director of Kensington Market Community Land Trust, and Steve Sirisko, Board Member of Arcadia Housing Co-Op.
Doors open: 6pm
No registration required.
The episodes are provided courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada.

title: TechTalk (In-Person) - November 2026
description:
Toronto JavaScript
Here’s the November edition of our Tech Talk event at Super.com on November 24, 2026.

Join us for some drinks, snacks, and Tech Talks.

Make sure to mark your calendars, come out, and join us for this event!

**🕑 Agenda & Schedule ✨**

* 18:00 - Doors open

* 18:20 - Intro and announcements

* 18:30 - **Attention Attention Everywhere** by **[Dev Shah](https://x.com/busycaesar)**
*Abstract:* In modern AI transformers, "attention is all you need"—but what does it actually compute? Demystify the mechanism step by step using real numbers. Learn why tokens split into queries, keys, and values, and verify the math against real GPT-2 weights, including why heads focus on token #1. A technical walkthrough.

* 19:00 - **Create an AI agent with Vercel AI SDK** by **[Emily Xiong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xiongemi/)**
*Abstract*: In this session, I’ll share how I "vibe coded" a custom AI Code Reviewer using Next.js and the Vercel AI SDK. We will break down the core capabilities of the Vercel AI SDK, comparing its unified approach to the manual overhead of using direct LLM APIs like OpenAI or Gemini.

* 19:30 - **Beyond Motion Generation** by **Karin Fam**
*Abstract*: AI can now generate an animation in seconds, but generation is the easy part. The real challenge starts when motion needs to ship consistently across dozens of screens, platforms, and teams.
In this talk, Karin looks at what comes after the prompt: how to think about animation as a system rather than a one-off asset, why scale and governance matter as much as creativity, and how teams can build motion workflows that stay consistent, performant, and on-brand as they grow.

* 20:00 - Networking

* 21:00 - Doors Close

(**Note**: *All times in the schedule are an approximation.*)

title: 🏀 Huskies vs. Phoenix: Basketball, Wings & Good Company!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
# 🏀 Huskies vs. Phoenix: Basketball, Wings & Good Company!

You don't have to be a sports fanatic to enjoy a good basketball game! Sometimes it's about cheering on a friend, getting out for the evening, and having some fun with a great group of people.

We're heading to George Brown College's St. James Campus to watch the **George Brown Huskies take on the Fleming Phoenix** in a college basketball matchup.

I have a personal connection to both the game and the school: George Brown is my alma mater, where I graduated as a Child and Youth Worker, and a friend of mine coaches the Fleming team. So I'm heading out to support my friend and enjoy an evening of basketball.

Come join me!

🏀 **The Game Plan**

* **6:30 PM:** Meet outside the main doors of George Brown College's St. James Campus. Look for my Moose Hat!
* **6:35 PM:** We'll head inside and make our way to the gymnasium. There may be other activities happening before tip-off, so we'll get settled and see what's going on.
* **7:00 PM:** Tip-off! Let's cheer on the teams and enjoy the game.
* **After the game:** We'll head over to St. Louis Bar & Grill on King Street for wings, food, and conversation. This part is completely optional, so you're welcome to join us for the game and head home afterward.

I'll wait five minutes at our meeting spot before heading inside, so arrive on time if you want to come in with the group.

🍗 **Why Stop at Basketball?**

The best part of getting together is often what happens afterward. Whether you're a basketball fan, a George Brown alum, or someone who just enjoys meeting new people, this is a chance to share an experience, have a few laughs, and make some new connections.

**A few things to know:**

* **No Meetup fee!** (Free event, real commitment!)
* Food and drinks afterward are optional, and everyone pays for their own order.
* You don't need to know anything about basketball to join us. Enthusiasm, curiosity, or a willingness to enjoy the evening is more than enough.

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This group is for people who want to be social, make friends, and enjoy time together — whether single or partnered.
We organize movies, walks, hikes, restaurant outings, arts and culture events, karaoke, and plenty more.

👤 **Organized by Mathew.**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**.

Come for the basketball, stay for the wings, and leave with a few new connections! 🏀🍗

title: ABCD Reads Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. End of life planning can be a daunting task, especially for the queer community. Participants will learn important factors to consider when doing their own end of life planning, review key documents, and talk about what to expect when working with a funeral director when a death occurs. Ezra Salter (they/them) is a Louisiana licensed Funeral Director and Embalmer practicing in New Orleans. They are co-creator of the Louisiana LGBTQ+ End of Life Planning Guide. Their professional focus includes advocacy for queer deathcare, green burial options, and the preservation of historic cemeteries. In their personal life they are a proud leatherdyke working to build local leather community. ‍

title: Canadian Writers in Person Reading Series: We, The Kindling
description:
Students get up close and personal with an eclectic group of authors while earning course credit through LA&PS’ Canadian Writers in Person (AP/CLTR 1953 6.0A) course. They explore the contemporary work of renowned authors, while having the unique opportunity to engage with them in a dialogue about their work.
Readings are free and open to members of the public and to members of the York community not enrolled in the course.
Our lineups consist of a unique selection of emerging and established Canadian writers, whose writing explores a broad range of topics, and a variety of geographical and cultural landscapes. Featuring seasoned and emerging poets and fiction writers, the series highlights Canada’s ever-growing literary talent.
November 24th – Join us for a live reading of We, the Kindling with Otoniya J. Okot Bitek tells the story of three women who survived abduction by the Lord’s Resistance Army in northern Uganda as children. Now adults, they struggle with the lasting emotional and psychological effects of their traumatic pasts while trying to build new lives and families. Through vivid storytelling, folk tales and multiple women’s voices, the novel explores war, survival, memory, trauma and the strength of human connection. Ultimately, it is a moving and powerful story about resilience, love and the lasting impact of violence.https://www.yorku.ca/laps/huma/canadian-writers/ ( https://www.yorku.ca/laps/huma/canadian-writers/ )

title: Civic Meetup #570: "Invaders,” “Polluters,” and “Predators”: Anti-South Asian Racism in Canadian Far-Right Digital Networks
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom
description:
Topic: "Invaders,” “Polluters,” and “Predators”: Anti-South Asian Racism in Canadian Far-Right Digital Networks

How do Canadian far-right groups portray South Asians on social media? Drawing on data collected from Canadian far-right networks on X (formerly Twitter), the analysis focuses on depictions of South Asians as “invaders,” “polluters,” and “predators,” and explores how emotions like fear and disgust are used​​ to frame South Asians as outsiders and perceived threats to Canada.

‎

Speaker: Dr. Zeinab Farokhi (in-person)

Dr. Zeinab Farokhi is an Assistant Professor of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at the University of Toronto Mississauga. Her upcoming book, Digital Islamophobia,  explores the gendered and affective dimensions of anti-Muslim sentiments across Canada, the United States, and India.

‎

Agenda:

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

7:50-9:00 Breakout groups

‎

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

Come and be part of it!
