title: Jan 14 - MCP, Agents and Skills Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Jan 14, 2027
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/mcp-agents-skills-meetup-january-14-2027)**

**From Demo to Production: Testing, Scaling and Securing AI Agents with Spring AI**

Your agent works perfectly in the demo. Then in production it gives a wrong answer and nobody can tell why, token costs spike, it slows to a crawl under load, and it calls a tool the user was never allowed to use. Building an agent is the easy part; the real work is running it like any other production service: tested, observable, scalable and secure.

Spring AI lets you do that with the Spring idioms and tooling you already know. This code-first session grows one example step by step. We start with a simple ChatClient, add advisors, memory and RAG, comparing the options Spring AI offers for each, and then let the agent act through tool calling and MCP.

Then come the production questions:

* Testing: we catch regressions with LLM-as-judge evaluators and typed decision models like Jev for fast, cheap verdicts.
* Observability: we add Micrometer traces, logs and token usage across model and tool calls.
* Scaling: we compare options for handling more concurrent users, from self-hosting to a managed runtime such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
* Security: we use Spring Security to authenticate users and make sure only the MCP tools they're allowed to use ever get called. You'll leave with reusable Spring patterns for agents that reason and act, and the discipline to test, observe, scale and secure them in production.

*About the Speaker*

[Andrei Shakirin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andrei-shakirin/) is a Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services and a former Pivotal Labs engineer, specializing in the design of highly scalable systems and generative AI applications. He is an active committer to several Spring and Apache open-source projects, contributor into MCP java SDK and a regular speaker at technical conferences.

**From Model Evals to System Evals: Evaluating Agents, Harnesses, and the Evaluators Themselves**

Every team shipping agents is quietly standing up two systems: the agent harness that plans, retrieves, calls tools, and edits code — and the evaluation harness that decides whether any of it can be trusted. Most teams only evaluate the first one's final output.

That is not enough. An agent can produce a correct answer through an unreliable, wasteful, or out-of-policy execution path, and outcome-only checks will pass it. This talk argues for evaluating the whole agent system: execution trajectories — tool correctness, evidence and grounding, state handling, policy compliance, and efficiency — alongside final outcomes, using deterministic specification checks an agent cannot game, model-based judges, and human-calibrated benchmarks.

We separate capability evaluations from regression evaluations so harness or model changes can be gated in CI. Then we turn the lens around: the evaluators themselves need evaluating — LLM judge calibration, disagreement analysis, and where human review still belongs.

Attendees leave with a production checklist for gating agent, model, and harness changes on system-level evidence instead of final answers.

*About the Speaker*

[Dipen Chawla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dipen-chawla-bb4a49bb/) is an AI engineer and researcher working on agentic AI systems and their evaluation, including agent memory and clinical diagnostic reasoning work at Microsoft, and data platform engineering at Walmart and S&P Global.

**Leading an Army of AI Agents**

Our AI coding agents now pick up tasks, follow team playbooks, open pull requests and wait for review. This firsthand engineering case study follows more than ten agents running in parallel and shows how briefs, shared context and verification loops keep their work reviewable.
It covers the failure modes too: confident wrong turns, incomplete verification, review bottlenecks and the attention required from human leaders.
Attendees will learn a practical task-to-PR workflow, how to make trust conditional on evidence, and which measures expose the costs hidden by faster output. The focus is on agent workflow and operating discipline, with concrete engineering examples rather than a product pitch.

*About the Speaker*

[John Adib](https://www.linkedin.com/in/MrAdib) is a London-based engineering manager at Zapp, a former CTO and two-time founder with 18+ years of software experience.

Agents in Action: Putting AI Agents to Work on Visual AI Data

What should an AI agent remember, and what should it forget? In this talk, we’ll explore the Voxel51 agent through the lens of memory, examining how retaining the right context and incorporating feedback can help agents improve over time. Through examples from visual AI workflows, we’ll discuss what’s worth remembering, from dataset context and user preferences to corrections and successful approaches, and when to update or discard information that becomes outdated. We’ll also explore how feedback and evaluation can help us determine whether an agent is making better decisions, offering practical insights for building agents that become more useful with experience.

*About the Speaker*

[Adonai Vera](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adonai-vera/) is a Machine Learning Engineer and DevRel at Voxel51 with over 7 years of experience building computer vision and machine learning models using TensorFlow, Docker, and OpenCV.

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe Opening Reception
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Artist Talk Sachiko Watanabe will share the story of ai (indigo), from growing plants to making dye material, demonstrating the traditional tools and techniques used to transform indigo plants into dye. Through her artwork and personal experiences, she will discuss the various indigo dyeing methods, her deep connection with nature, her lifestyle and the role that love and care play in her creative practice. The presentation will include: An introduction to the cultivation of indigo, the preparation of natural dye, and the artistic process behind her work. A video presentation showcasing her life, practice and creative journey. A Q&A session with the audience. Exhibition info Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. Living in a traditional Japanese house, where she also exhibits and sells her work, Sachiko continues to work closely with indigo each day. Through her textiles, she hopes to share its quiet beauty and to remind us of the natural world that surrounds and embraces us. Her exhibitions include Indigo in Our Daily Lives (2019), Indigo, Simultaneously (2021), Indigo in Winter (2021), Indigo in Darkness (2022), and Intaking Indigo (2024) Photo: © Toshinori Tanaka

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
For over twenty years, Sachiko Watanabe has lived with indigo — growing it, fermenting it, dyeing with it, and shaping her days around its rhythms. Traveling from her home in Japan, she brings this quiet, deeply personal practice to the JCCC for the first time. Rooted in one of Japan's oldest natural dyeing traditions, natural indigo sukumo fermentation, this exhibition invites you to slow down and step into her world — to see, touch, and feel the colour of a life shaped by patience, land, and time. Join us in welcoming her to Toronto. About the Exhibition The exhibition follows the full life cycle of indigo — from seed to sukumo, from vat to fabric, from field to everyday life. Visitors will encounter: The Making of Sukumo — a year-long journey through sowing, transplanting, harvesting, drying, and fermenting indigo leaves Shades of Indigo — a study of the many named hues within the indigo spectrum, from pale aijiro(藍白) to deep kachi-iro(搗色) Textiles & Objects — a curated collection of dyed khadi, cotton, linen, hemp, and wool pieces, shaped by Sachiko's hand Everyday Indigo — an invitation to touch, smell, and wrap yourself in indigo cloth Living with Indigo — a reflection on more than twelve years spent in an old farmhouse, where growing, fermenting, and dyeing indigo have become inseparable from daily life Opening Reception & Artist Talk Please join us on January 16 at 2pm More Info Workshops Details coming soon! Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. title: ABCD Reads The End of Everything by M. John Harrison
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads [The End of Everything](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4802129) by M. John Harrison, winner of the [2026 Booker Prize](https://thebookerprizes.com/the-booker-library/prize-years/2026).

([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6285142977675264) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Phillip Tennent makes his living at the tideline, collecting artifacts that wash up from the Channel. It's been years since the crisis changed everything, but its exact nature remains obscure. Government barely functions, the seas are full of new creatures, an entire continent has been mislaid. It feels like the end. Now Phillip has fished out of the water an object he can't keep. A creature that keeps changing. An artifact he must take inland, before it destroys everything he thinks he knows." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/the-end-of-everything/))

"The End of Everything is a slyly satirical and unsettling post-apocalyptic adventure into the limits of human understanding from the peerless master of contemporary fiction." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/245886309-american-hagwon))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

location: Live on Zoom @ Zoom
description:
This workshop is designed for graduate students and postdoctoral scholars who want to strengthen their ability to navigate ethical challenges in research and professional practice. While responsible conduct of research is often presented through policies and regulations, researchers frequently encounter situations where the “right” course of action is not immediately clear. These complex scenarios require thoughtful judgment, critical reflection, and the ability to articulate and defend ethical decisions.
By the end of the workshop, participants will have greater confidence in navigating ethically challenging situations and a stronger foundation for responsible leadership in research and professional environments. The skills developed are relevant across disciplines and career paths, supporting participants in becoming thoughtful, reflective, and ethically grounded professionals.

title: Belonging: A Sense of Place : 6-Week Art Therapy Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee, for a six-week closed art therapy group for adults!
Belonging: A Sense of Place invites participants to slow down, connect with nature, and explore their inner world through creative expression. Each session includes a brief meditation, gentle check-in, nature-inspired art-making, and optional sharing.
 
Across the six weeks, the garden becomes both a setting and a metaphor for exploring themes of memory, identity, place, belonging, relationship, and what makes somewhere feel like “home.” Each session introduces a distinct theme while contributing to an overarching exploration of belonging and our relationship with the natural world.
 
As a closed group, participants are invited to attend all six sessions. The continuity of the series offers opportunities to build trust, develop connections, and deepen reflection as the sessions unfold.
 
The group is facilitated by Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee who creates gentle, creative spaces that support reflection, care, growth, and connection. Art therapy uses the creative process as a way to explore emotions, experiences, relationships, and self-awareness, with no emphasis on artistic skill or producing a finished artwork.
 
Wednesdays, January 20 through February 24, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. (six sessions).
Public $120, TBG Members $90 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.

description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Aimi Kobayashi Piano Recital
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Experience an unforgettable evening with acclaimed Japanese pianist Aimi Kobayashi, celebrated for her “perfect technique, a light touch, fast and virtuoso” playing. A Fourth Prize winner at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition, Kobayashi has captivated audiences around the world with her exceptional artistry, expressive depth, and extraordinary musicality. From her early beginnings at the age of three to performances with leading orchestras across Japan and Europe, she has established herself as one of Japan’s most sought-after pianists of her generation. Her distinguished career includes performances with the Orchestra of the Eighteenth Century, Moscow Virtuosi, Yomiuri Nippon Symphony Orchestra, Japan Philharmonic Orchestra, New Japan Philharmonic, Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich, Tokyo Symphony Orchestra, and Münchner Philharmoniker. Her recordings for Warner Classics feature works by Bach, Beethoven, Chopin, Liszt, and her latest album, Schubert (2024). Join us for an inspiring evening of piano artistry as Aimi Kobayashi brings her remarkable talent and passion to the stage. Concert Program: Beethoven: Bagatelles, Op. 126 Chopin: Nocturne in F major, Op. 15, No. 1 Chopin: Mazurka in F minor, Op. 68, No. 4 Chopin: Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23 Schubert: Piano Sonata No. 20 in A major, D. 959 *Concert program subject to change. Tickets $65 General Admission $50 JCCC Members and Bravo Niagara! Members $30 25 years old and Under Notes: HST not included no refunds/exchanges Tickets co-presented by the JCCC and Bravo Niagara! In Montreal, at the dawn of the 20th century, a poor boy falls in love with a girl whose sorrow turns into pearls. He sells them to a ruthless pawnbroker, who hungers for more. Tempted by greed, the boy must choose between love and fortune. The choice could damn his soul.
The 2026 Oscar® Winner for Best Animated Short Film from the acclaimed team of Chris Lavis and Maciek Szczerbowski. This meticulously crafted film is a testament to the magic of stop-motion animation. With handmade puppets, mesmerizing narration by Colm Feore and a haunting score by Patrick Watson,
The Girl Who Cried Pearls
is a timeless parable of desire, deception and the price of innocence. (25 minutes)
Also screening from the same Oscar winning team with be
Higglety Pigglety Pop! or There Must Be More to Life
. This live-action/animated adaptation of Maurice Sendak's book features the voices of Meryl Streep and Forest Whitaker.
The story follows Jennie the terrier's suspenseful and unexpectedly moving journey to gain new experiences and realize her dream of becoming the star of the World Mother Goose Theatre. (23 minutes)
Films courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada (NFB).

title: Tea Time Talk: Mental Health Matters
location: 305 Founders (Senior Common Room) @ 99 Ottawa Rd, North York, ON M7A 2C5, Canada
description:
Health is about more than how we feel physically. Join Student Counselling, Health and Well-Being for a warm conversation exploring the six dimensions of well-being, what mental health really means and how it supports us as students and in everyday life, especially during the dark, cold winter months.
We’ll talk about the winter blues and simple ways to care for your mental health, then create your own Winter Wellness Kit— a personalized set of tools and feel-good strategies to take home.
Grab a cup of tea, bring your questions and let’s talk about mental health in a way that feels real, supportive and fun.
Light refreshments provided
Open to all York University Students
Date: Wednesday, January 27th, 2027
Time: noon – 1:30 p.m.
Location: Founders College 305
You are welcome to drop in, but registering helps us make sure there are enough refreshments and supplies for everyone.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: VCP presents BIPOC ARTIST HUB SHOWCASE
location: Fred Thury Studio Theatre, 258 Vanier College
description:
Vanier College Productions (VCP) is excited to continue with the first-ever BIPOC Artist Hub at York University. Open to all BIPOC artists (theatre, dance, music, film, visual art, design, writing, etc.) at York, the group meets every Tuesday from 4:30-6:30pm. Now in its sixth year, join us for discussions, creative collaboration, and help bring our annual showcase to life.
Starting in September, students from VCP’s BIPOC Artist HUB will be working towards bringing a themed arts showcase to life.
This year, patrons and audiences can get an exclusive look at the featured art exhibits, in advance of the showcase! In January, stop by Vanier College, Room 001 between 9am-4pm, Monday-Friday, to catch all the amazing artwork on display.
Want to see more from the HUB? Join us for our BIPOC Artist HUB Showcase happening Jan. 28-30. With exhibits that range from visual art, board games, live performances, and more, we hope to transport you to other worlds with our personal stories, reflections and ideations.

Please note the author will be available after the event to sign copies of his book.
Please register online.

title: I Cheerfully Refuse by Leif Enger
description:
Post-Apocalyptic Book Club - Toronto Chapter
This time we'll be reading *I Cheerfully Refuse* by Leif Enger. Here's the blurb:

Set in a not-too-distant America, *I Cheerfully Refuse* is the tale of Rainy, an aspiring musician setting sail on Lake Superior in search of his departed, deeply beloved, bookselling wife. An endearing bear of an Orphean narrator, he seeks refuge in the harbors, fogs, and remote islands of the inland sea. After encountering lunatic storms and rising corpses from the warming depths, he eventually lands to find an increasingly desperate and illiterate people, a malignant billionaire ruling class, a crumbled infrastructure, and a lawless society. As his guileless nature begins to make an inadvertent rebel of him, Rainy’s private quest for the love of his life grows into something wider and wilder, sweeping up friends and foes alike in his wake.

description:
The Faculty of Graduate Studies is hosting a session entitled Digital Research Tools for Doctoral Success. Join us!
Doctoral research involves managing complex projects, vast amounts of information, and evolving workflows. The right digital tools can help researchers work more efficiently, stay organized, and make the research process more manageable. This session explores practical tools and strategies for citation management, note-taking, collaboration, writing, project planning, and organizing your research workflow. Participants will learn how digital approaches can support effective research practices and help develop sustainable systems for navigating the demands of advanced scholarship.

Time: 12:00-1:00 p.m. (ET)

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

🛡️ **Community Guidelines:**
Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

location: 152 Founders Assembly Hall, Founders College
description:
Looking for a fun way to connect with other first-year students and spread a little positivity this semester? Join us for LA&PS Love That for You! 💖
This Valentine’s-inspired celebration is all about friendship, self-care, and creating meaningful connections in a welcoming and inclusive environment. Drop in to meet new people, take a break from your studies, and enjoy an afternoon filled with feel-good activities designed just for LA&PS first-year students.
Get creative by making Valentine’s cards, crafting colourful pipe-cleaner flowers, and exploring other hands-on activities. Capture memories with friends at our photo booth, and spend some time with therapy dogs for the ultimate stress-relieving study break.
Of course, there will also be free food, snacks, and plenty of opportunities to relax, socialize, and enjoy the positive vibes. Whether you come with friends or arrive on your own, you’ll find a welcoming community ready to celebrate kindness, connection, and belonging. Stay for the whole event or drop in between classes, we’d love to see you there!
We can’t wait to celebrate with you! 💕✨

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Common Hour: Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence featuring guitarist Rez Abbasi
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall Accolade East Building, York University @ 4700 Keele Street
description:
The Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence program at York University brings renowned jazz musicians to the Department of Music each year for multi-day residencies featuring student workshops, masterclasses, and a culminating public performance.
Award winning guitarist, Rez Abbasi ( https://www.reztone.com/ ) is featured as part of the Department of Music’s 2026-2027 Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence.
The following session is free and open to the public.
Date: Thursday, February 11
Time: 12:30 – 1:30 p.m.
Location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall
Free Admission
REZ ABBASI
Guitarist, composer, author and 2021 Guggenheim Fellow, Rez Abbasi is among a rare
breed of artists that continue to push boundaries from within the traditions he has
embraced. Consistently placing on DownBeat magazine’s International Critics Poll in
Guitar alongside luminaries Bill Frisell and Pat Metheny since 2014, Abbasi continues to
forge new ground with his multi-dimensional projects.
“Abbasi is living, breathing proof that jazz music can be as vital and boundary-pushing as
ever.” AllAboutJazz.com.
Born in Karachi, Pakistan, migrating to Southern California at the age of four, schooled
at the University of Southern California and the Manhattan School of Music in jazz and
classical music, along with a pilgrimage in India under the guidance of master
percussionist, Ustad Alla Rakha, Abbasi is a vivid synthesis of all the above stated
influences and genres.
“Mr. Abbasi succeeded in making some fairly cerebral intricacies feel intuitive and
touched by a higher purpose.” – New York Times
The Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence is made possible by a grant from the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.

title: Learn to Grow Native Plants From Seed: Sowing In a Winter Wonderland
location: Cliffcrest
description:
Who says you can’t grow a garden in the winter? Winter sowing is an easy and inexpensive way to start native seeds. Through this simple method of sowing seeds during the colder months, you can plan your garden to support butterflies, bees and birds.
In this workshop, learn how surprisingly easy it is to grow native wildflowers from seed if we follow nature’s lead by embracing the cold!
In this presentation, Dorte Windmuller, a Butterflyway Ranger of the David Suzuki Foundation, will lead a hands-on experience of seed cleaning and packing. Participants can take some seed packets home for your garden or balcony.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile
Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Thailand Sea Side Discovery: Bangkok, Phuket and Krabi Island
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join us for an unforgettable 10-day Meetup adventure through Thailand, blending culture, temples, islands, beaches, and relaxed free time. This trip is a true Meetup - designed for those who want to travel the world and explore exotic destinations like Thailand, but don’t want to do it alone. We are traveling as a group, while still enjoying flexibility and optional experiences.
This journey blends the energy of Bangkok, the tropical beauty of Phuket, and the laid-back charm of Krabi, creating the perfect balance of culture, nature, and downtime. We will explore iconic temples, cruise through stunning islands, relax on white-sand beaches, and enjoy free time to wander, shop, or simply slow down and soak it all in.

**Trip Highlights**
• Bangkok City & Temple Tour
• Optional Ayutthaya Day Trip
• Flight to Phuket included
• Phi Phi Islands Tour
• Big Buddha Visit
• Scenic drive from Phuket to Krabi
• 4 Island Hopping Tour with Picnic

**Who is this trip for**
✔ Solo travelers who don’t want to travel alone
✔ People who want structure without feeling rushed
✔ Travelers who enjoy a mix of sightseeing and free time
✔ Anyone who wants to experience Thailand with a fun, supportive group

This adventure is ideal for solo travelers, friends, couples and even families, who want the comfort of a group while keeping the experience fun and social.

TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

title: Get the Jump on Spring 2027
location: ON
description:
Where the Plant People Meet



Shake off the winter blues and start the countdown to spring at Toronto Botanical Garden’s much-loved Get the Jump on Spring one-day garden extravaganza. Whether you’re a seasoned gardener, a curious beginner, or simply dreaming of warmer days, this annual event brings together plant lovers, expert growers, and local makers for a joyful, inspiration-packed kickoff to spring. 



Saturday, February 20, 2027, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.FREE Admission. $2 suggested minimum donation 







What to Expect













Plant Community Connections 



Meet fellow plant enthusiasts, swap stories, ask questions, and connect with horticultural societies, plant and seed vendors, local makers, and other community groups dedicated to gardening, nature, and sustainable living. 









Over 40 Local Makers & Eco-Vendors



Discover unique houseplants, organic seed vendors, botanical-inspired products, garden accessories, natural wellness items, and artisan goods from over 40 local makers and growers. 









Interested in Participating in 2027




APPLICATIONS FOR VENDOR SPACES IS NOW OPEN














Visit the Plant Doctor



Have questions about the health or care of your indoor plant(s)? Looking for help on how to repot your plant? Bring in your plant(s) or a photo, and our horticulturists will provide you with an on-the-spot assessment and treatment. Examples of services offered include: Pruning, repotting, leaf cleaning and pest removal. 



Please note: If your plant is HEAVILY infested with pests, you should keep it at home and only bring in a photo. This service is ideal for small or young plants. We will not be able to help you unload/load your plant. 









Free Plant & Seed Swap



Bring as many plants as you wish to trade. If there isn’t anything of interest on the table when you arrive, add your plant(s) and take a ticket to redeem later when you see something new you’d like to try.  



Drop by the Weston Family Library, which houses our Seed Library. You can borrow seeds for FREE! If you have extra seeds, package and label them to add to our seed library collection. There will be a seed library assistant to assist you with your selections and contributions. 















Seasonal Plants & Seed Sales



Shop a curated selection of seeds, unique plants, and specialty offerings from trusted growers—perfect for getting a head start on your garden plans. Drop by the Garden Shop to learn more about our new online plant shop with at-home delivery, pre-order early-blooming hellebores, and sample a flight of local Ontario honey. 









Pop up Plant Cafe



Recharge with a coffee, tea, or freshly baked cookie, square, or scone. Gluten-free, Dairy-free & nut-free options available. Bistro seating is available. Operated by Daniel et Daniel. 















Free Garden Chats



Grow your gardening confidence with interactive sessions in the Weston Family Library led by the Toronto Master Gardeners. No registration required. 









Free Family Fun



Bring the whole family along! Kids can enjoy a drop-in, plant-themed craft to take home or, if you prefer a quiet moment, roast marshmallow over the outdoor firepit or simply relax together and cuddle with a book in our cozy indoor corners. 














Ways you can make this event more sustainable




TBG will have waste stations for reuseable, recyclable and compostable materials with hands-on volunteers to assist.



Bring your water bottle and take advantage of our complimentary water station, bring your mug, plate, or cutlery.



You are encouraged to bring your reusable bags or boxes to carry your seeds, plants, or garden-related treasures home.









How to get there



Click here for directions and parking information.

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

title: Global Philosophy Research Interest Group Talk (Jeannie Miller, University of Toronto)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Global Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Jeannie Miller, an associate professor in the Department of Near and Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Toronto. Her book, The Quibbler: Al-Jahiz’s Equivocations in Kitab al-Hayawan and Beyond is a study of the Arabic writings of al-Jahiz, a foundational 9th-century author and analyzes al-Jahiz’s literary style and unique voice as a performative demonstration of good thinking, according to his definition. She is currently working on several interconnected studies of the reception and afterlife of Abbasid texts in premodern Islamicate contexts, using manuscripts as evidence. How were these texts read before the modernizing movements of the 19th and 20th centuries and the advent of a modern notion of “literature”?

title: Galapagos Islands Expedition ~ Untouched Nature in all its Splendor! Small Group
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
***It's a Meetup . . . in the Galápagos!!***

**This Meetup Event is for the nature lovers, for the curious explorers and the adventurers who want to experience nature in all its splendor & diversity.**

The Galápagos Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean, considered one of the world's foremost destinations for wildlife-viewing. It's a place where lizards swim, birds walk, and humans — for once — don't take center stage. In 1835 a 26-year-old Charles Darwin introduced the Galápagos Islands to the world with his theory of evolution.

As amazing as you think the Galápagos Islands would be, they exceed all expectations of our group in 2023 and 2025! That sea lion above in our group photo is not a prop! It was very real, ready to play and pose for a picture. You can see sea lions, giant lizards and many other exotic and friendly creatures, waddling on the streets, playing in the sand or just chilling (sun bathing) on a bench!

***We will explore and experience:***

* The famous Galapagos penguin and blue footed boobies. Swim with sea turtles and sea lions.
* Tortuga Bay Beach for swimming, snorkeling, kayaking or surfing with unique marine life.
* Get close and personal with the giant tortoises roaming in their natural habitat
* Explore the Tintoreras islet, home of the white tip sharks and its shark tunnel.
* Visit the Charles Darwin Station, to observe giant tortoises and their babies and learn about this majestic animal.
* Snorkeling around the shore of the Tijeretas Bay
* Boat ride to Kicker Rock with snorkeling
* Sailing to Santa Cruz Island.
* Sail to Isabela Island, the largest of the archipelago.
* Boat tour to Tuneles De Cabo Rosa, a formation of series of above ocean arches, creating an unique snorkeling experience.
* Explore cavernous underground Lava Tunnels.
* Tour the Galapagos rainforest habitat
* San Cristobal Island with visit to the Interpretation Center
* Visit to Los Gemelos, a haven for bird watchers!
* Visit Sierra Negra and Chico Volcano. A 10-mile challenging hike (for those who are interested)
* El Trapiche to see the old methods of extracting cane juice, roasting coffee beans and techniques of distillery.
* Quito with a full day tour and visit to the Equator line
* Visit to the town of Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

💬 WhatsApp Group Chat: [https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

🛡️ **Community Guidelines:**
Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

Come for the conversations, stay for the community! 🌎💬❤️

title: Postgres Conference 2027: Celebrating 20 Years of Community & Innovation! 🐘🎉
description:
Toronto Postgres
Join us as Postgres Conference turns 20! We are marking two decades of community-driven database excellence by gathering developers, DBAs, architects, and maintainers from around the globe who build, manage, and scale Postgres in production.

**📍 Venue:** San Jose Marriott, San Jose, California
📅 **Dates:** Apr 21, 2027 – Apr 23, 2027

**Two Decades of Real-World Engineering**
Reaching this milestone is a testament to the strength and resilience of open source engineering. Our community continues to push data systems forward, from core protocol advancements and a thriving extension ecosystem to autovacuum tuning, vector workloads, high availability, and data security.

## **Interested in Speaking? 📢**

Help shape our 20th anniversary program! We invite practitioners, researchers, and community members to submit speaker proposals. Share your hard-won production lessons, architecture strategies, security and compliance insights, post-mortems, or technical benchmarks with our global audience.

## **Conference Tracks**

Our comprehensive, multi-day, multi-track program offers deep technical sessions and holistic professional growth:

* **Essentials:** Fundamental concepts, best practices, and foundational knowledge for new and growing Postgres users, including secure configuration and access control basics..
* **Dev:** Application design, ORMs, query optimization, advanced SQL features, and secure coding practices such as preventing SQL injection and using row-level security.
* **Ops:** High availability, replication, backup & recovery, performance tuning, and infrastructure management, along with hardening, encryption, auditing, and compliance.
* **Extensions:** Extending Postgres functionality, custom extension development, and ecosystem integration, plus security tooling like pgaudit and extension supply chain safety.
* **AI:** Vector embeddings, pgvector, LLM integration, AI-driven data pipelines, data sovereignty, governance, and protecting sensitive data used in AI workloads.
* **Professional Development & Wellness:** Career growth, engineering leadership, mental health, and maintaining work-life balance.
* **Life & Fun:** Community stories, creative technical pursuits, and social networking activities.

**How to Submit Your Proposal**
Ready to share your knowledge with the Postgres community? Submit your proposal at [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new)

**Visit the official conference portal to learn more about Postgres Conference 2027:**
**👉 [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027 ](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027)**

**Questions?**
